An important player for the Swedish giants, frustration over his rumoured departure has boiled over in recent weeks, with the player audibly booed by sections of the club’s support during the warm-up against Gothenburg recently. Signed for £5million from Hansa Rostock last January, he struggled to impress at Ibrox initially, but has exploded into life this season, scoring nine goals and assisting a further five in 17 games across all competitions.

Taking full advantage of his chance after injuries to Lawrence Shankland and Youssef Chermiti saw him allowed to lead the Rangers frontline, his prolific form has not gone unnoticed across the border, with EFL Championship promotion chasers West Ham United and Wolverhampton Wanderers reported to be mulling over a megabucks deal in the new year, alongside an unnamed team from the German Bundesliga.

According to a report from TEAMTalk, both Naderi and Rangers teammate Olwethu Makhanya have been scouted at Ibrox in recent weeks. Currently on a 12 game unbeaten run in all competitions, however, it is understood the club has no intention of allowing any of their star men to leave in January, with the Ibrox hierarchy determined to ensure they don’t disrupt their momentum mid-season.

#2002. Milan Futuro 3-0 Virtus CiseranoBergamo: Pandolfi shines in third straight win

It was a clean sweep for AC Milan’s men’s teams over the weekend, as Milan Futuro won their third straight in the league.

The Futuro got back in the win column last weekend as they managed to secure a thrilling 3-2 victory away against Virtus Verona on Sunday. Then, they followed that up by beating Piacenza 2-1 in midweek, in the game that had been suspended due to an injury to the referee.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

So, there was some good momentum for the second team heading into Sunday afternoon’s game, and they built on it with a commanding and convincing 3-0 home win over Virtus CiseranoBergamo.

Fabio Pandolfi opened the scoring just after the half-hour mark as he finished from close range after an excellent assist from Aurelien Guernier on the right, making it 1-0 which is how it would stay going into the break.

Early in the second half, Pandolfi got his second after a deflected left-footed shot wrong-footed the goalkeeper Rovelli and nestled into the net. In the closing stages, Cappelletti led a counter-attack and squared to Yahya Idrissi-Regragui, who made no mistake and made sure of the win.

#2001. ‘I do worry’ - Sky Sports expert gives Brighton title verdict amid Arsenal claim

Brighton could be the "nearest pursuers" to Arsenal for the Premier League title, according to Sky Sports pundit Don Goodman.

The Seagulls have made an impressive start to the season and are second on 22 points after 10 matches.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Fabian Hurzeler's men are five points adrift of leaders Arsenal and one ahead of third placed Manchester City.

Brighton are also the leading scorers in the division with 26 goals and have conceded just seven times - only Arsenal have leaked fewer with five.

"There is an argument to be made that they would be the nearest pursuers to Arsenal," said Goodman, speaking to Betway.

"But I can’t see them sustaining the results that they’ll need to in order to overtake Arsenal, and the reason is Arsenal have already got a five-point cushion on Brighton.

"In terms of the rest of the teams though, they do seem to be the ones that are putting it together the best."

Brighton do have a strong squad this season but Goodman feels the demands of the Premier League and Uefa Conference League could catch up with them in the later stages.

He added: "I think winning the league might be a fraction beyond them though, and I do worry later on in the season what impact juggling European football will have on Brighton.

"When you look back to last season and you saw that Crystal Palace, Nottingham Forest and Spurs were all in a relegation battle.

"I do think that this season it looks like Sunderland for example are struggling juggling that European football with Premier League football, so it’s not uncommon.

"For Brighton to be able to sustain it through a 38-game Premier League season and a European campaign, you kind of think maybe not win the league, but absolutely, you hope that they can be challenging for a top-four Champions League spot."

Goodman, who had a prolific career as a striker for the likes of West Bromwich Albion, Sunderland and Wolves, has been impressed by the rise of Brighton and believes it’s just reward for how the club operates and long-term planning.

“I’ve been commentating for Sky Sports for 20 years next March, and I’ve commentated on Brighton and Hove Albion in League One and a lot in the Championship over that period of time,” Goodman added.

“To see the progression of the football club, along with others like Bournemouth and Brentford who are very similar in terms of the trajectory is wonderful and highlights the benefit of being a forward-thinking, well-run football club that plans ahead.

“It is wonderful to watch football clubs progress, and I think that over the last certainly few seasons since the Europa Conference League has been introduced by UEFA, it has certainly provided a happy hunting ground for Premier League clubs in terms of being able to win it.

“And there’s no reason whatsoever that Brighton cannot go on to win the Europa Conference League.

“I’m not saying it’s easy, but I’m saying with the football that they’re playing, you could make an argument that they’re the best team in it.”

#2000. Andy Robertson: My 102 caps is a chance to recognise what Sir Kenny Dalglish did - not me

Scotland captain Andy Robertson claims his 102nd cap should be a reason to celebrate Sir Kenny Dalglish and not himself as he prepares to join his fellow former Liverpool player as record appearance holder.

The 32-year-old will draw level with Dalglish when he leads Scotland out at Hampden on Friday against North Macedonia in the Nations League.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

“Tomorrow’s not really about me,” the Tottenham left-back said. “It’s about him in my opinion. For how long the record stood, for what he achieved in his career, for the person he is.

“It’s another reason for our country to tip our hat to one of the greatest players that have played the game, never mind in Scotland, he’s definitely the greatest in Scotland.”

Robertson was speaking on the 40th anniversary of Dalglish’s final international, a 3-0 win over Luxembourg when he was in his second season as Liverpool player/manager.

“That tells you everything that you need to know, the fact that he’s juggling all that and still showing up for his country,” Robertson said. “He reminds me all the time that 102 caps back then was a lot harder than 102 caps now, and he’s right because there were less games.

“In terms of numbers, I’ll stand side by side with him, but I don’t want people to forget how important this man has been for our country. He was arguably the best player in the world at his time and he’ll always be the greatest in this country.”

Dalglish recently joked that he hoped Robertson would retire before he sets a new record. “We’ve had a lot of jokes, but I also know deep down how proud he is of me and how happy he is for me as well,” the former Dundee United player said. “I always remember when I got the captaincy, he was one of the first people to text me and say, ‘I know I’ve been out of the game maybe a little bit, but if you need help, if you need somebody to bounce anything off, then I can be that person’.

“To have somebody like that, that you can bounce anything off and rely on, him and his family have been such a massive help to my family, especially in my time at Liverpool.

“I’ve got no doubt there’ll be a couple of texts that will get exchanged. I know we laugh and we joke, publicly and privately, but I know he’s proud of me and he’s happy for what I’ve achieved as well.”

Robertson is set to surpass Dalglish in Switzerland on Monday and he is no mood to slow down. “I’m still hungry to achieve more for the country,” he said. “I want to get Scotland back to another major tournament, I want to try and get out the group stages.

“Secondly, I want to try and leave the squad in the best possible place in terms of the quality coming through, the characters they’ve got, the mentality they’ve got.

“If I can leave that behind, then I can maybe enjoy Scotland games a bit more and I can join the fans and party with them.”

#1999. New Bromley boss Karl Robinson heaps praise on 'megastar' Jermain Defoe - with Premier League legend in talks over dugout return after walking out on Woking

Published: 08:00 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 13:33 EST, 7 November 2026

New Bromley boss Karl Robinson has hailed Premier League 'megastar' Jermain Defoe as the ultimate professional following his abrupt departure from Woking.

Daily Mail Sport revealed on Tuesday that Defoe is in talks to join Robinson's backroom staff at League One strugglers Bromley after Andy Woodman's dismissal last month.

And while his appointment has yet to be confirmed, Robinson jumped at the chance to wax lyrical about Defoe at his inauguration on Thursday.

Bromley sit bottom of League One but their new boss believes Defoe's meticulous attention to detail would help the players find another gear.

'There's been a lot of talk but there always is with names like Jermain Defoe, who is a megastar. He's one of the greatest Premier League strikers of all time,' Robinson said.

'I have to raise and change the narrative of what this stands for,' the new boss pointed to the Bromley badge on his jumper.

Jermain Defoe is in talks to join League One strugglers Bromley as Karl Robinson's assistant

Former Salford City manager Robinson has hailed 'megastar' Defoe as the ultimate professional

'I have to bring people in to make me the best version of myself. I spoke to people who know Jermain and played with him.

'He was always first in. All the players who have played with him will tell you that. Steven Gerrard will tell you that.

'He was first in and still in the training ground at 4pm - massages, recovery, gym, video analysis of the players he's playing against.

'I was speaking to him about something completely different the other day and we were talking about discipline and professionalism.

'I said to him: "what do you do that for?". He went: "If I do everything right Monday to Friday and I play poorly, I can accept it because I've done everything in the week to be the best version of myself."

'I'm listening and I've got goose pimples on my arm. Then I'm thinking, that's probably why you're Jermain Defoe, because he did everything he possibly could to maximise his talent.

Defoe has been out of work since walking away from National League side Woking after just four months at the helm amid a strained relationship with the club's director of football.

The 44-year-old took charge of the final six games of last season and was expected to lead the club into the new campaign.

However, he failed to report for work on the eve of the season before contacting the club later that day to inform them he would not be returning.

The former England international and Tottenham Hotspur striker would add top-level experience to the dressing room, having scored 163 Premier League goals in 496 appearances - ranking 10th on the Premier League's scoring charts.

Robinson spoke as though he idolised Defoe when quizzed on his potential appointment, highlighting his humility and relentlessness as key assets to succeed as a coach.

'Failure isn't falling short, it's when you don't maximise your talent. And I think some of the players here haven't maximised their athletic, technical and tactical capabilities', Robinson added.

'For whatever reason, we need to find the key to what that is. I think someone like Jermain (would bring that) because he maximised everything he was and everything he is.

'That's almost the secret behind the genius of the top players. It's their attention to detail, professionalism and discipline – he does that over and over again.

'He's tried to manage in non-league as well. That, in itself, is dropping your ego to learn.'

Although Bromley are still working on finalising Defoe's appointment, he is expected to join Robinson in the dugout at Hayes Lane. The Ravens host Rotherham in the first round of the FA Cup this weekend as Robinson takes his first game in charge.

It will be the first clash between them in Edinburgh this season and in a communication to their fans, Celtic revealed that they have been given approximately 20 per cent less tickets than is usually the case.

#1996. Cisse discusses humble beginnings, choosing Milan, Italy call-up, Amorim and amazing form

Alphadjo Cisse has shed some light on his journey to becoming an AC Milan player, as well as what his first few months at the club have been like.

It has been a simply remarkable rise for Cisse, who at the start of 2026 was playing in the second division with Catanzaro, on loan from Hellas Verona. Milan bought him from there but left him with his loan club, before a serious injury needed surgery and ruled him out for the rest of the season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Fast-forwarding to early November, and the 20-year-old is currently the top scorer for the Rossoneri with eight goals, the most recent of which came in Sunday’s 2-1 win over Genoa. There is talk of an imminent renewal already, while Roberto Mancini gave him a senior Italy call-up.

Cisse gave an exclusive interview to Cronache di Spogliatoio in which he touched upon various topics from his upbringing to the brilliant moment he is currently experiencing. MilanNews relayed his words.

“My life changed in my father’s factory. A Verona manager went to meet him at work to beg him to take me to their place. He’d been a worker forever: every day he’d leave work at 5:00pm, and by 5:15 he was already outside our house, calling me and taking me to play soccer.

“I still remember the first time. It was afternoon. He came up to the house and said, ‘Come on, I’ll take you somewhere’. And we went to the pitch. He was the one who instilled in me the passion for soccer, and from that moment on, I’ve never stopped.

“My parents made so many sacrifices to support me on this journey: my mom, when she had days off from work, would come up with me to take me on the bus to practice.”

“My mom is a very demanding mom. But she helps me stay focused and prevent fame from overwhelming me. So everything becomes easier with her. They tell me every day that they’re proud of me, but they also do everything they can to keep me grounded.

“Carlos, Milan’s assistant coach, often tells me this too: ‘ Surround yourself with people who truly love you and who help you stay focused’. I’m sure of this: I carry with me the carefree attitude of the child I was. I play with a smile. It’s hard not to have that in these first few months.”

You have just been called up by the Italian national team for the first time…

“I was on my way to do the pre-match interview against Ferencváros in the Europa League and they stopped me to say, ‘Alpha, they’ve called you up to the national team… the senior team!’ I had the match, I only realised afterwards.

“I want to prove I can compete. The call was in the air, they’d been talking to me about it for days… but this is my big chance. I haven’t had the chance to stop and think about my career. Football moves fast.”

“A few weeks ago, they asked me how much of my potential as a player I’d shown. I said 70%. Can I say that? Maybe I need to lower it a bit… let’s say 40%, because I have so many aspects to improve on, but at the same time, I know who I am and what I’m worth.

“Last season, Aquilani – who was my coach at Catanzaro – told me that ‘if you don’t play at least 10 years in Serie A, I think you’ll have failed’. I took it as a positive motivation, a phrase that pushed me to always do better and believe in what I can do.

“One of my friends in football is Favasuli, I met him just last year in Serie B. We often found ourselves talking… daydreaming. I still remember the day he said to me: ‘Think about when one day we’ll face two great teams’.

“I smiled. ‘It would be great to meet again in Serie A, but maybe it’s a little too late for me, I’m already 23…’ Instead, he made it too: Milan-Napoli will be in December, we’ll see. He was my driver, he drove me to camp. He’s proof that there’s no age to stop feeling young or believing in it, no matter the path.”

Your path has already taken you from Verona to Catanzaro and to Milan…

“In those very months, my life changed again. No longer in my father’s factory. In a matter of days, I had gone from wondering how far I was from Serie A to finding myself facing the most important decision of my career.

“I’ll be honest: I didn’t take that moment very well. When I arrived at Catanzaro, I had only played two five-minute games in Serie A, including against AC Milan. Aquilani and manager Polito really wanted me, they pushed me. It was my first experience away from home.

“In just a few months, I scored a lot, everyone wanted me. And in January, I was practically on a flight to Holland, bound for Rotterdam: to sign with PSV. But then AC Milan came along.”

“My friends’ WhatsApp group exploded: ‘Alpha, is it true?!’ And I was like, ‘Yes guys, yes!’ I didn’t want to make the wrong choice: PSV wanted me right away, while Milan would have let me finish the season in Serie B.

“Two great teams, but Milan… how do you explain that? I was experiencing a mix of emotions; my parents told me to stay calm and that the best was yet to come. We decided this was the right choice. And judging by how things are going, I’d say we were right.”

“The first few times I came to Milanello, I did so to recover from my injury. Milan left me at Catanzaro, yes, but after a few days I got injured. In fact, I had serious doubts: ‘I’m coming to AC Milan after an injury, let’s see how it goes’.

“This is exactly what Amorim spoke to me about as soon as we met. We focused on the injury, and he explained what he expected of me on the pitch. He’s a great guy, and he knows how to deal with us young players. And he knows how to keep me grounded. Even though I’m not someone who likes to let my mind wander.”

You kept a promise after your Europa League hat-trick…

“Even after my hat-trick in the Europa League, I have to say that everything was already clear to me: it was simply confirmation to myself that I can compete at this level. I didn’t see it as a point of arrival, but as a promise kept to the child I was.

“And above all, as a promise to keep. Even though I was coming back from a long injury, even though I’m young and have so many areas to improve, I never had any doubts about my abilities or where I could go. I’m very demanding of myself, just like my mother.”

“Modrić gave me some advice on what I need to improve: I need to read the game better and understand the moments of the match. He’s a great player, a spectacular person, willing to help you learn, and interesting to listen to.

“Even though my idol was very different as a kid: Paul Pogba, when he was at Juventus. We do different things on the pitch, and his haircut certainly didn’t go unnoticed by a kid… maybe I’ll get one in the future! What I appreciated about him was that he made people laugh: that’s what I want to do too.

“I was inspired by the player whose jersey I had as a child: Clarence Seedorf. My mother gave it to me; it was the one I wore on the pitch. So maybe it was just my destiny to come here. Seedorf became an idol at San Siro.

“The place where you feel the grandeur, the pressure, the feeling of playing in a stadium that represents a childhood dream. Being there now is like saying to the child I was: ‘See? You did it’. It’s a huge motivation for me. But I’m carefree enough not to be affected by it.

“When you start playing, you notice it less and you don’t pay attention: it’s easier. The fans are incredibly attached to the team. You notice it not just in Milan, but all over the world. And that’s how you understand where you are. I was really impressed by the organisation here.”

Do you like to play with a certain freedom?

“I’m very carefree when I go on the pitch. Whether it’s playing in Serie B or going to San Siro, I think it’s normal for me. I’m the same person I always am. As a kid, I was obsessed with bicycle kicks. I scored five or six incredible goals… now I avoid them!

“In the Verona youth team, I had a coach, Paolo Sammarco, who shaped the way I play today: he gave me a lot of freedom, helping me understand how I should express myself.”

Is it important for young Italian players to have confidence?

“Italy is full of strong young players, I assure you. It all depends on the opportunities you’re given. Many have emerged in recent months, including me, and I’m sure many more will emerge in the near future.

“When you reach a certain level, you’re amazed: one above all, I was struck by Pisilli, he’s simply amazing. I knew him, but when I played with him, I understood his strength. And I understood my own strength when, in my early years in Verona, I approached the big boys.

“The level was rising, but I continued to have faith, to understand that I could achieve great things if I followed the path I had. That I had something special.”

Your life has changed a lot, are you still the same person?

“My life has changed so much in the past few months, perhaps more than I can even realize. There are moments when I stop and think about how different everything is from just a short while ago. Football is taking me to places I dreamed of, but inside I’m still the same boy.

“But I know what my ambitions are. And perhaps that’s exactly what helps me not lose myself, even when everything changes. I try to enjoy every moment, without forgetting where I started from and all the people who have accompanied me to this point.”

Finally, clear something up: how do you say your name?

“My name is Cisse, without an accent. My name can be read any way, but it’s pronounced ‘Sisse’. I even had to send a voice message to the commentators!”

"We had no real continuity within any unit, but since we’ve been able to build relationships over the past six or seven weeks, things have started to come together.

"We’ve started to see some results, which is a reflection of the hard work the boys have been putting in. So it’s been difficult at times but we’ve managed to make it work and we’ve put a good group together.”

O’Neill said the highlights so far had been two down-to-the-wire wins. "One was at home to Faversham – we were 2-0 up, then it was 2-2 and we scored to make it 3-2 in the 90th minute, which was amazing.

"And then Herne Bay away, we were 2-0 up, it went to 3-3 and we scored with the last kick to win it. Those have probably been our best two wins.

"In terms of performances, our first away, away to Eastbourne Town, it wasn’t the nicest or the prettiest, but to get a clean sheet and defend the goal and our lead was excellent.

"Saturday’s win versus Horley was frustrating because we got caught up in a game that suited them. We started really well but got sucked into it.

"We had to work hard on Saturday and knew we would have to – Horley are fighting for every point, they’re fighting every battle so it was important we matched that.

"The squad is looking really good now. We’ve had a lot of injuries and suspensions but Saturday I think we only have one injury and one suspension so we have 16 players to choose from which is nice – against Horley last weekend we only had 13 available.

"We have a couple of additions coming in this week and hopefully they will boost us over the next eight weeks. But to come out of seven weeks of Saturday-Tuesday games and be where we are, we’re really positive.

“We can recover properly between games now from Saturday to Saturday so that’s positive and hopefully we’ll see a reflection of that in how we play and in getting more points on the board.”

O’Neill’s men visit leaders Hastings on Saturday – the Pilot Field men are second in the table although have lost their past three home games.

#1992. Chichester City blow hot and cold – but keep on battling

On Saturday goals from Harry Bridle and Lucas Pattenden earned a creditable 2-1 home win over Bath City, who had a man sent off just before the break. See David Richardson’s Chi City v Bath City gallery here.

But on Tuesday night at Chertsey, Ben Pashley’s goal just after the hour came when City were already 2-0 down and they couldn’t go on to rescue a point.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Three points from six have left City seventh, having won nine of their opening 17 games.

City now take a break from league action for a week. They visit National League South high flyers Salisbury in the second round of the FA Trophy on Saturday, then go to SCFL Premier side Hassocks in the third round of the Sussex Transport Senior Cup on Tuesday.

Manager Miles Rutherford said they were delighted to beat Bath – but frustrated not to get anything from the Chertsey trip.

“We’re still blowing hot and cold, but I think it’s the same for a lot of clubs in this league. Anyone can beat anyone, you’re seeing that in results,” Rutherford said.

“It was a good win on Saturday and Chertsey was a fairly even game. We were 1-0 down at half-time but should have been 2-1 up – we missed two glorious chances.

“We felt confident at half-time but started the second half poorly. When we did get one back we didn’t really build on it.”

Coach Darin Killpartrick said: “I felt we deserved to beat Bath. Their red card changed things but it was another excellent, entertaining game with two sides going at each other.

“At Chertsey, the effort from the players was excellent but on the technical side, we failed in some aspects.”

Rutherford admitted the current schedule was testing City’s small squad, with a number of players now injured – including Curtis da Costa, Ryan Davidson and James Sweet.

He said they’d go to Salisbury for Saturday’s Trophy tie as underdogs but determined to give it their best shot.

“We’re having to do a lot of travelling at the moment but we have to get on with it and try to grind out some results.”

Killpartrick said: “It feels like a pinch point of the season at the moment. We’ll get through it but we need all the support we can get.

“We had more than 600 at Oaklands Park for the Bath City and would love local people to keep coming and helping us grow the support. And we wouldn’t mind a nice coach for away trips if anyone wants to help!”

Here is Ian Worden’s match report from the defeat at Chertsey….

Chichester City might have been the better side but came away from Surrey with nothing from Chertsey Town.

Nathan Minhas scored on seven minutes after Will Sweet under-hit a back header to keeper Max Evans, and Daniel Berry made it 2-0 in the second half. Ben Pashley pulled one back for Chi on 63 for what would prove to be a consolation goal.

City made two changes to the starting XI which beat Bath City on Saturday. Skipper Rob Hutchings once again lined up at left back with Isaac Bello on the other side, partnering Pashley and Sweet, this time, in the centre of defence. Evans began as usual between the posts with Joe Moore, Emmett Dunn, Lucas Pattenden and Lloyd Rowlatt, given a start, in midfield behind top scorer Harry Bridle up front and Brandon Chebby who scored twice against Frome and earned the MoM award versus the other Somerset club at the weekend.

Moore cleared in the fourth minute of play and Evans collected a forward pass from Darryl Harrison as the Curfews attacked the Signature End. Chebby won the first corner of the night at Alwyns Lane after Hutchings’ pass was deflected. Rowlatt took this but Pashley headed over.

The hosts took the lead early doors through Nathan Minhas. Bridle spurned an opportunity to level things up almost immediately at the Eden Gate end and Joe Grant dragged a shot off target 60 seconds later.

Both sides exchanged throws in the next passage of play before Rowlatt, who shone at the weekend in his cameo, won the visitors a free kick. Top scorer Bridle had another go 11 minutes in but couldn’t get a decent connection.

Next, Pashley’s straight ball didn’t pick Pattenden and the Chi midfielder had a cross cut out before Bridle, on 16 goals this season in all comps, fired narrowly over the bar. Minhas’ burst of pace gave him some space, although he played a disappointing pass looking for his teammate Berry.

Pattenden then saw his shot blocked in the 18th minute and Minhas picked up a knock. Dunn headed clear a long Curfews’ throw and Eoin Casey was booked for fouling Hutchings at the mid-point.

Chertsey keeper Luke Roberts gathered Bello’s pass towards Pattenden before Hutchings and Chebby hooked up down the left flank, although Bridle’s flick was easy for Richards.

A lovely touch from Rowlatt set him up for a ball that didn’t quite find a marauding Chebby, and Pashley cleared Berry’s delivery as the home side pressed again. Pattenden’s cross/shot wasn’t turned in by Bridle on the half hour mark and Evans comfortably saved a shot by Berry as things swung this way and that.

Then Minhas tried to curl one but Evans denied him easily enough before Darryl Harrison was fouled on the edge of the penalty area and Dunn was booked. Berry was adjudged to have hand balled on 37 but Hutchings’ set-piece got headed away and Evans met the ball before Berry.

With five minutes of the first half to go Pashley beat Minhas and Dunn was fouled by Wayne Ridgely – no yellow card according to referee Adam Steele. A bit of Chuckle Brothers stuff between Bello and Pattenden didn’t work out and Town countered and won a corner which the Lillywhites’ back-line cleared.

Evans claimed a Conor Lee effort without any trouble and on the stroke of half time Chebby could have/should have gone down in the box but he won a corner that came to nothing as Mr Steele blew for the break.

Rowlatt was subbed at the interval for Worthing loanee Burgess and Ridley came off and got replaced by Leo Farruch. Pattenden went down and received some physio treatment after barely a minute and Chebby did Casey but Hutchings’ cross was too deep.

Then Roberts got to it ahead of Bridle on 50 minutes before Hutchings headed the ball out for a Town corner which Chebby hacked away. And it was 2-0 in the 53rd minute when Berry headed home, and Chebby won the visitors a corner that Sweet blazed off target.

A Hutchings’ foul on Lee led to a free kick which Chertsey captain Alex Fisher took, and Evans comfortably saved the consequent header. Next, Isaac Olorunfemi pulled the trigger but it was miles off and Pashley pulled one back for the Sussex side on 63 minutes with a header from a City corner.

Pattenden was beaten to the ball by a defender and Roberts in the 66th minute as Chichester sought an equaliser. Farruch then fired an attempt wide of the mark; Bridle was flagged offside; and Pashley blocked the follow up shot when Hutchings got done.

Bridle couldn’t get his feet right and had an effort saved for a corner on 73. Sweet did well up against Minhas in the 74th minute, and Dunn thought he had won a corner but the ref gave a Curfews’ goal kick. Moments later Pattenden crossed although City couldn’t profit from it before Olly Munt was introduced for Joe Moore.

Sweet tried to find Pattenden on 82 minutes but Roberts gathered and both Bridle and Bello had chances blocked – the second one for a Chi corner. The two teams exchanged set pieces in the following spell and Bridle earned Chichester a corner.

Then it was easier to score then miss for Grant but he somehow missed his second bite at the cherry with two minutes of normal time to go. Hutchings couldn’t keep his shot down in the 89th minute and Clarke replaced Sweet.

The ref added seven minutes of additional time and nice skill from Chebby won Chi a corner that Hutchings delivered for another on the other side. Try as they might Chichester just couldn’t find a leveller as the game drew to a close.

Chichester City: Evans, Bello, Hutchings, Moore, W. Sweet, Pashley, Dunn, Pattenden, Rowlatt, Chebby, Bridle (Munt, Clarke, Burgess).

#1991. Osmand proves he's no Honda Civic... and now he's ready to motor on for Celtic

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:00 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 13:48 EST, 7 November 2026

When Brendan Rodgers returns to Glasgow for a Q&A session next June, it would feel like a waste of time for him to be grilled on the exact reasons behind his team selection for matches which, by then, will have taken place almost two years ago.

Frankly, those assembled in the Royal Concert Hall that evening will have their mind on other matters.

Nonetheless, there remains a curiosity about why the Northern Irishman overlooked Callum Osmand at a time when Celtic were evidently crying out for a spark up front.

Rodgers, you may well remember, had spoken with great excitement about the club signing the player from Fulham a few weeks previously.

Sure, Osmand was only 19 at the time. He hadn't played a single minute of first-team football, either.

But as a combination of Daizen Maeda and the soon-to-depart Adam Idah failed to find the net across 210 minutes against Kairat Almaty, you couldn't help but wonder if the much-vaunted teenager stationed on the bench in both legs might have been worth a shot.

Despite Rodgers giving Osmand the big build up that summer, the forward didn't play a single minute prior to his abrupt departure at the end of October.

While that was clearly his prerogative, the impact Osmand has made across an injury-stricken year does suggest that it was an oversight.

Handed his debut as a substitute by Martin O'Neill against Falkirk soon after, Osmand scored a brilliant flashing header in the League Cup semi-final against Rangers before sustaining a serious hamstring tear against Midtjylland.

Only back in contention on the final day of the season after surgery, he set up Maeda and scored himself as Celtic clinched the title in dramatic fashion against Hearts.

Having been sidelined again with an ankle injury at the outset of this campaign, he's rebounded in some style. His goal and assist for Camilo Duran against Besiktas on Thursday came a couple of weeks after scoring twice in a 7-1 rout against the Tynecastle men in what was his first senior start.

Callum Osmand made an instant impression off the bench against Besiktas

After just 13 matches for Celtic, it may be a little too early to describe Osmand as a Ferrari. But a Honda Civic, he is most certainly not.

The beauty of the situation, from the club's perspective, is that the player hasn't even revved the engine as he sets out on his career path.

Osmand, who turns 21 as Kilmarnock visit today, looks first-team ready any time he's taken the field. Yet he's the first to admit that the game-time those injuries denied him stunted his development.

Provided there's a fair wind at his back, though, he's certain there's a lot more to come.

'I would say I'm nowhere near where I want to be personally,' he said.

'There's stuff I need to tidy up on, like decision-making and all this stuff.

'But I feel like the more games I play, the more I understand and the more I learn.

'So, on a personal note, that's what I'd want to do - just keep learning and keep understanding my role within the team and obviously the players you're playing with.

'I've still only played a handful of games, so it's tough learning. But I feel like when you get thrown in the deep end, it's the best way to learn. You learn more off the worst games than the good games.

'It's just as long as I can get better every game, that's all I really want to focus on.'

There's no doubt, though, that there are many moments when he looks the real deal.

For instance, his brilliant finish after Callum McGregor's square ball on Thursday, his first touch after coming off the bench.

'It was crazy,' he smiled. 'It's a surreal feeling when it's my first touch as well.

'I was a bit nervous that I'd shanked it, but no, I'm happy that I caught it nicely.'

One of his next involvements wasn't too bad, either. Motoring into space off the left flank, Osmand had to find the perfect weight and direction on the pass which would allow Camilo Duran to exploit a pocket of space and round the keeper. He could not have played it better.

Osmand has struck up a good understanding with fellow Celtic striker Camilo Duran

'I thought he was offside, to be honest,' he recalled of the moment in which Celtic moved 2-1 in front.

'I was looking at the bench saying 'Close?' and they were like, "Yeah, it's tight".

'But I know where he's going. He's such a sharp striker, so I know if I put that in the space, the keeper is not getting anywhere near it. He's a top, top player, so I can't fault him at all.'

With all due respect to Colby Donovan – also assured after coming off the bench – Thursday night will long be remembered for the belated contributions of Osmand and Duran, who scored three goals between them.

The Colombian began on the right flank, but moved infield once Kasper Hogh tired. The understanding Duran had with Osmand was clear throughout and ultimately proved the undoing of the Turks.

'He's unbelievable, a really top player,' Osmand said. 'You can just see even by the way he walks and the way he moves.

'I learn off him every day. He's an amazing guy. His English is really not great, but somehow we manage to talk to each other a lot.

'I think I find him quite a good friend of mine now.

'And although we might not speak many words, you can tell just by looking ... I don't know how to describe it. Like we talk to each other a lot. Maybe it's little words, but I feel like we get on really well. He's a great guy.'

Duran's finish at the second attempt to seal the victory later on felt hugely significant for all associated with Celtic.

It was precisely the kind of big win at the right moment which O'Neill and his embattled squad needed to blow away the storm clouds. On such moments, entire seasons can hinge and reputations are forged.

'For us, it felt like a must win, like that was our sort of mindset going into that,' Osmand said.

'I think the boys did amazing, so hopefully we just get some confidence and build on from this and that gives us confidence to play more free and take more risks.

'Sometimes when you're not as confident, it's tough to play the football you want to play.'

#1990. Bognor Regis Town bosses lay down challenge ahead of Littlehampton Town’s visit

That’s the over-riding take from manager Danny Hollands and his assistant gaffer Ben Kneller as they prepare their troops for the game against the struggling Marigolds at Nyewood Lane.

It’s third from top against second from bottom; but Kneller insists that form goes out of the window when it comes to derby matches.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The Rocks lost last time out 2-1 at Windsor & Eton and before that suffered a home defeat at the hands of Egham Town – but despite those reverses they are still in contention at the right end of the standings.

But it is imperative that they find a way of winning against the side bossed by Mitch Hand and George Gaskin.

Kneller says his hope is that the players will put the disappointment of the past couple of results behind them, dig deep and go again against visitors who will be keen to get one over on the Rocks after Hollands’ men’s 1-0 win in the reverse fixture earlier in the season.

He said: "Littlehampton are going to provide a challenge, we know what they are going to be like, but again we have got to be brave. Any derby, across any country, in any city, form is irrelevant -- it's going to be about who is going to roll their sleeves up and have a go and that's where we are going to be.”

And he has asked the Green Army to play their part by raising the roof in support of the players in a bid to help them try to get over the line and secure a victory.

He added: “Two defeats on the spin, you just want to get a win; there is going to be some spice to it but we are at home... there was 1,600 here last season (for the same fixture) so hopefully it will be similar and we need to get the fans to get behind the boys. It’s Littlehampton so there is a little bit more on the table and they are scrapping for their lives.”

Assessing the Windsor result, he said: “Disappointed after a very, very bright start and I thought this is nice, zippy pitch, nice and flat and then we go 2-0 down with two mistakes. But it is what it is. In the second half we have come out and hit the bar three times.

“Cal (Laycock) has been unfortunate as the keeper has made a couple of saves. Then we should have had a stonewall penalty. We have had a reaction but we have come away with nothing, so disappointed from our side of things but we can't keep giving ourselves mountains to climb unfortunately.

“We've got to be braver but it's a dip in form and it is what it is, we have got to stay bright and we will. Happy with the reaction but disappointed where we were at half-time.

“Cal has come back in after a long lay-off, Pards (Luke Pardoe) isn't himself because he has been out for 10 weeks, so it is hard for him and he is getting frustrated. Ollie Lovell has come back, he is a big player for us, Charlie Wassmer is still in the stands... so no excuses, we are capable.

"Once we get a full squad back -- and maybe a couple of ins and a couple of outs -- we will be okay. If we said at the start of the season come November where are we going to be, we are going to be third, just off the top, you'd have settled for that. We just need to regroup and keep pushing.”

#1989. Cisse like the greats, Amorim surpasses Allegri: All the key stats from Genoa 1-2 AC Milan

AC Milan won their seventh Serie A game of the season on Sunday afternoon, beating a Genoa side that entered the game in great form.

The home crowd at the Marassi were fired up going into this one given Genoa had won four of their last five. However, goals from Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic inside the opening 20 minutes was exactly what Milan needed to take the ascendancy.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ellertsson did score inside the final few minutes as Genoa mounted a late surge in the hopes of snatching a point, but the Rossoneri held on to win 2-1 and move back into the top four places in the table.

Looking at the general stats makes for interesting reading. Milan dominated the ball with 62% possession, but Genoa had nearly double the Expected Goals (1.14 to 0.61), even though big chances ended up being even at two apiece.

The Rossoblu also had nearly triple the shots (17 to 6) and shots on target (5 to 2), while the Rossoneri did not win a single corner. It suggests that Ruben Amorim’s side simply took their moments and sat back, though maybe Daniele De Rossi can feel a bit hard done by.

📊 The stats from the win against Genoa. pic.twitter.com/wr1E6cohcZ

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 8, 2026

Alphadjo Cisse is one of only three players born in 2006 or later to have scored 8+ goals across all competitions in Europe’s top five leagues. The others are Lamine Yamal (13) and Paris Brunner (8).

In terms of minutes per goal in Serie A, Cisse leads the way with one every 81 minutes. That puts him ahead of the likes of Donyell Malen (one every 82), Lautaro Martinez (one every 88) and Gustavo Varela (one every 91).

After 13 appearances for Milan, Cisse is level with Filippo Inzaghi, Andriy Shevchenko and Alberto Gilardino on 8 goals. Pierino Prati (10) and Mario Balotelli (12) are the only players to record more.

Milan are unbeaten in their last 11 Serie A matches against Genoa (W7, D4). Since 2020-21, the Rossoneri only have a longer run of unbeaten games against Hellas Verona (12).

The Diavolo have won each of their last five Serie A away games against Genoa. Only against one team do the Rossoneri currently have a longer running away win streak in the competition: Hellas Verona (seven).

Milan have won three and drawn three of their first six away games this season. The Rossoneri have pnly avoided defeat in their first six away games of the season on three occasions between 2020-21 and 2025-26, the same number as Inter and Napoli, and could now become the only team to do so four times in this span, including the current season.

With this victory, AC Milan climbed to 24 points in the standings, two more than the number earned by Massimiliano Allegri’s Milan last season after 11 games. This is also better than Stefano Pioli’s last season, also by two points.

#1987. Senegal vs Sudan - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 10 Nov 2026 23:08, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 10:22

Senegal host Sudan in Group J of 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying at Stade Leopold Sedar Senghor in Dakar on Thursday.

The Lions of Teranga are unbeaten but have scored only twice in two games, while the Falcons of Jediane arrive third on three points after a 4-1 defeat in Maputo.

Senegal are second in Group J on four points, level with Mozambique but behind them on goal difference, +1 to +3.

Patrick Vieira's first competitive game in charge ended 1-1 away to Mozambique on September 25, and Senegal then edged Ethiopia 1-0 in Bahir Dar four days later through Ibrahim Mbaye's 11th-minute goal despite 61% possession.

The 1-0 friendly win over Comoros in Marseille on October 4, settled by Iliman Ndiaye's fifth-minute goal, made it three games in a row with a single Senegal goal and only one conceded across them.

Off the pitch, Ismail Jakobs has retired from international football, and Sadio Mane asked to be excused from the squad to stay home with his family.

Vieira's second squad includes four first call-ups, Pathe Mboup, Pape Demba Diop, Clayton Diandy and Paul Mendy, and does not include Idrissa Gana Gueye.

Senegal have not lost in eight meetings with Sudan, winning five and drawing three, the latest a 3-1 victory in the Africa Cup of Nations last 16 in Tangier on January 3 in which Pape Gueye scored twice before half time.

Sudan are third in Group J on three points with two goals scored and four conceded, and both of their goals have come from penalties.

Mohamed Eisa converted an 86th-minute penalty to beat Ethiopia 1-0 in Juba, the capital of South Sudan, on September 25, a result that briefly took the Falcons of Jediane top of the group.

Mozambique then won 4-1 in Maputo on September 29, with Witi scoring in the 24th minute, Chamito adding a brace, Guima making it 3-0 in the 58th minute and Yaser Hamed pulling one back from the spot in the 88th.

Kwesi Appiah, the Ghanaian head coach, took Sudan to the last 16 of the January tournament, where Abdallah, a semi-professional at an Australian second-tier club in Melbourne, gave them a sixth-minute lead before Senegal replied three times.

Several of Appiah's players come from Al Hilal and Al Merrikh, and the return leg against Senegal follows on Monday, November 16.

Mamadou Sarr is out with a left calf injury sustained in Real Sociedad's 1-1 Europa League draw with Lyon, and the club has indicated he will miss at least two to three weeks.

Krepin Diatta was forced off in Watford's Championship match against Middlesbrough on November 7 and has been replaced in the squad by the Sevilla defender Arouna Sangante.

Habib Diarra, Ismaila Sarr and Abdallah Sima are also unavailable, which leaves Nicolas Jackson, Mbaye, Ndiaye and Boulaye Dia as the main attacking options.

With Jakobs retired, El Hadji Malick Diouf is the left-back option, and Kalidou Koulibaly captains a back line that also includes Moussa Niakhate.

For the visitors, no injury or suspension has been reported ahead of the trip to Dakar.

Mohamed Eisa and Yasin Hamed have found the back of the net from the spot against Ethiopia and Mozambique respectively, and will hope to get a goal from open play against Senegal.

Senegal's three straight one-goal games are the genuine concern, but Sudan conceded four in Maputo and three in Tangier in January, and Jackson and Mbaye combined for the winner in Bahir Dar.

Absences such as Mane, Diatta and Sarr thin the squad, yet the Koulibaly and Niakhate pairing remains intact and should be enough to keep out a Sudan attack whose only goals so far came from the penalty spot.

#1986. Sebastien Pocognoli must take next Scotland step - especially with two key reinforcements

There was a certain amount of grace afforded to Sebastien Pocognoli’s first international break as Scotland manager.

Back in September/October, Scotland played four Nations League B1 matches across three weeks - defeating North Macedonia in Skopje, drawing with Slovenia in Ljubljana and losing at home to Switzerland and the Slovenians.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

A new voice, a new style and some new players. Debuts were given to defenders Stephen Welsh, Luis Binks, Luke Graham, winger Josh McPake and striker Robbie Ure. The likes of Oli McBurnie returned. A fresh formation was implemented. Pocognoli’s Scotland looked very different to his predecessor, Steve Clarke.

The change has largely been welcomed amid criticism of a stale style under Clarke. And up until the visit of Slovenia in the final match of the quartet, there was optimism that Scotland were going in the right direction. The 2-1 reversal by the visitors, however, leaves Scotland in an unenviable position in this group. Finishing second is the best Pocognoli can hope for, and that would require at the very least taking four points from North Macedonia and Switzerland in the final two matches.

Last time out, four points on the road was pleasing. The 3-0 defeat by Switzerland - World Cup quarter-finalists, it must be stressed - could be partly explained by an early red card for Jack Hendry. The performance against Slovenia at home raised concerns, though, with Scotland too open, fatigued and meek in the final third.

Pocognoli knows that at the very least in this international fortnight, Scotland must beat North Macedonia at Hampden on Friday. The Balkan nation are toiling, have not taken a point so far and looked bedraggled when Scotland vanquished them. It would breathe some confidence into the team ahead of Monday’s trip to St Gallen, where Scotland will face a Swiss side that may already have top spot sewn up.

Finishing second would require positive results in both fixtures. Doing so would be significant, as it would make Scotland second seeds in next month’s Euro 2028 qualification draw.

What is more feasible is improvement from Scotland. While the team certainly played with more adventure and gumption, there remained a lack of ruthlessness in the final third. Kieron Bowie scored his first goal for his country, but McBurnie remains strike-less after 20 appearances. Perhaps the North Macedonians will be more accommodating.

Pocognoli is able to replenish his forward line with two important members of the Scotland squad for the past few years. Torino striker Che Adams missed out last time due to a muscle injury, but he is fit and firing in Serie A, having scored four goals this season. Often asked to plough a lone furrow under Clarke, it will be fascinating to see how he thrives in a more forward-thinking set-up - and potentially with a partner up top.

Adams’ return is welcomed but there can be no doubt that Pocognoli will be most excited to work with Scott McTominay. The 29-year-old talisman was ruled out of the first camp with a minor heart issue but after a successful operation, he has returned to Napoli and while Gli Azzurri are toiling in mid-table, McTominay has netted five goals and remains front and centre of their best work.

Competition in the midfield area remains fierce. Shoehorning McTominay, John McGinn, Billy Gilmour, Lewis Ferguson and Ryan Christie into one team has always been a challenge and will be even harder if Pocognoli decides to stick with two strikers - which he should do against opposition of North Macedonia’s calibre. A combination of Adams and McBurnie in attack seems likely, especially as Bowie has not been starting regularly for Sassuolo.

Gilmour became front and centre of Scotland’s midfield in the last international window and was Scotland’s main source of vertical creativity. McGinn and Ferguson started every game - and both are in good form with their clubs. At Bologna, Ferguson tops the charts in Serie A for distance covered (114.1m), total passes (817) and accurate passes (754). Christie and Bournemouth are flying. These are nice problems to have.

Scotland looked jaded by the second match against Slovenia and while this break is shorter, there is an argument for more rotation. And there will have to be changes in defence, given Welsh and Binks have been forced to withdraw from this squad, replaced by forgotten men Ryan Porteous and David Bates, while Scott McKenna is also absent.

Pocognoli operated with a back three but may be minded to change given the absentees and porousness against stronger opposition. While Porteous has fared well in the States with LA, Graham - often a starter for Stoke City - may be ahead of him in the international pecking order. Kieran Tierney withdrew from the last squad, but is fit this time around and can play as a left-sided centre-half.

Captain Andy Robertson will move level with Sir Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps should he be, as is expected, deployed on the left flank. There is more debate on the other side. Winger Ben Gannon-Doak could give Scotland more oomph in a game they have to win than Aaron Hickey and Nathan Patterson.

There’s even debate with the goalkeeper. Angus Gunn’s status as an untouchable No 1 waned a little on the back of performances last month. Could in-form Falkirk stopper Scott Bain oust him?

Pocognoli has options, that’s for sure. The Tartan Army will want to see Scotland more secure tactically. There needs to be a step forward in this brave new world. And while winning in Switzerland may prove a step too far, landing a first home win under the 39-year-old Belgian feels non-negotiable.

North Macedonia at home was the sort of match Scotland gobbled up in the past. This may be a new regime, but that particular old habit must die hard.

But he has reminded his players they need to show hard graft as well as their footballing qualities in each upcoming match – whether they’re playing National League big names or step five neighbours Wick in the Sussex Senior Cup.

#1984. 'This club's not used to losing' - keeper Johnstone opens up on Celtic struggles

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:00 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 13:48 EST, 7 November 2026

Sam Johnstone has warned that Thursday's dramatic win over Besiktas must be seen as just the first step on Celtic's road to recovery.

The pulsating 3-2 triumph over the Turks came after Martin O'Neill's men had lost four straight matches in Europe with just three wins in the previous ten matches in all competitions.

As timely as the result was, the keeper believes there's a lot of hard work for the side to get through before anyone can talk about it being a turning point in what's been a trying season to this stage.

Asked if the spirit in the camp had been affected by a string of adverse results, Johnstone said: 'Of course it has. I think the results affect it.

'This club's not used to losing and we've probably lost too many games for this club.

'We all realise that, but we have to put things right in each game.

'The lads go out to win every game, so the camp's good.

'It was tough. We're honest players, we're honest people and honest with each other.

'You could see on Thursday night that the lads put a good fight in and got the result.'

Signed on loan from Wolves for the season, Johnstone was handed his chance by O'Neill only to drop out of the team following an indifferent display in the 3-0 loss at Ibrox on September 13.

Celtic goalkeeper is finding his feet in Scottish football after a difficult start

But having been selected ahead of Viljami Sinisalo in the past five matches, the former England goalkeeper believes he's steadily making progress.

'To get a run of games for any player, you find your rhythm,' Johnstone explained.

'It was a new club for me, a new team, so that takes probably a couple of games to get used to as well.

'I think I've got to get used to them (defenders), they've got to get used to me and that only happens through playing and through games. It's great to be in the team.

'It's good. I love playing. It's a great team to play in, a great club to play for and we keep taking it game by game. We go again on Sunday.'

Johnstone moved to Celtic at the start of a difficult period which saw the side struggle for consistency.

Adamant that he's never regretted moving up to Scotland for a minute, however, he added: 'The expectation, rightly so, for this place is to win games.

'Unfortunately, we hadn't quite met that expectation and the lads know that.

'Like I said, we try to win every game and put things right.

Celtic fought back for a much-needed Europa League victory against Besiktas

'It's brilliant to play for this club. The passion of the fans, good and bad. The standard of players on the pitch, day in, day out at training.

'When I came, I said I didn't have to think twice about coming here.'

Having heard so much about Celtic Park on the night of a big European win, the keeper was glad to finally witness it for himself.

'It was unbelievable to experience this place, rocking and get the win,' he reflected.

'It's a great feeling. It's great to play in front of and feel the passion of the fans. That does help the lads and drives the lads on.

'As you could see, there were times in the game where we struggled a little bit, but the lads dug in. It's never going to be easy.

'In the Europa League, you're playing top teams and, after last week's result as well, we were under a lot of pressure. The lads came up with the goods.

'We've still got a chance to qualify, and that's our aim, so we'll take the next game the same as any other game, that we go to win.'

Nelson said of the Rooks fans: “They're unreal. We always try to repay them regardless of what the score is, but here feels a little bit special.

“Even at the beginning of the season, they all talked about Dulwich away and making sure we can come here and put out a performance they can go home and be proud of, and they were noisy.

“[Tyler] Cox came over to me and said, ‘They've been unbelievable. I can't wait to get back on the pitch just to clap for them,’ and that's what it means. They were our 12th man, and it's a pleasure to be able to stand in front of them with three points.”

With their trip to Enfield having been rescheduled to a Tuesday night, Lewes had an uphill task against a side in title contention.

The Rooks began their season with a 4-0 loss to the North London side, and while they started much better on the road, reaching half-time at a stalemate, the hosts’ quality eventually won out.

“I think we're looking at the champions of the league,” said Nelson.

“I felt we had to ride a lot of waves in the first half, but we dug in to keep it nil-nil, and then ran out of luck.

“It's probably the first time I've stood in front of you guys and said that we were totally outplayed, outclassed, outmatched, outrun, and outduelled. So I think you can't ever stand on the other side of that and expect to get anything from the game.”

Another busy week awaits the Rooks, with a home meeting with Isthmian Premier Division basement club Stanway Rovers this Saturday (3pm kick-off) before a Sussex Senior Cup trip to Eastbourne Town on Tuesday night (7.45pm).

#1981. Sky: Ramos involved but has minimal support – the numbers that illustrate Amorim’s point

Some interesting analysis on AC Milan and Goncalo Ramos’ attacking struggles has been provided by the Sky studios.

It was a familiar tale for Ramos during Milan’s 2-1 win over Genoa on Sunday. He was involved but rarely inside the box, then he was selfless instead of ruthless in front of goal when he chose to square for Christian Pulisic to make it 2-0.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The worries are starting to grow regarding whether the Portuguese can provide the output required of a number nine that cost €70m. Yet, the Rossoneri have scored 23 goals in 11 league games which suggests goals are coming from elsewhere, sometimes with Ramos’ help.

Sky offered some interesting insight after Sunday’s game. Firstly, they picked out just how involved Ramos actually is with various aspects of Milan’s overall play.

For example, he is first among Serie A strikers for interceptions and recoveries, while he is second for receptions, touches and duels. He is third for passes.

He is first among centre-forwards in the league for touches in the middle third of the field and touches in the opposition half. He is second for fouls committed plus fouls suffered among forwards, with 41.

Sky then shift the focus to the team’s overall play to try and explain why Ramos perhaps isn’t getting the quality service and is having to drop deeper as a result.

They look at data per 30 minutes of possession. Milan are first in Serie A for build-up actions, but they are 20th for entries into the final third and entries into the opposition box.

Amorim’s side are 19th for percentage of touches in the attacking third and 18th in percentage of touches in the opposition box. With numbers like these, there isn’t much for Ramos to get on the end of.

What does this tell us? Well, Amorim’s post match assessment about struggling to get the ball from the defensive third into the final third are true. Milan have a lot of the ball but still struggle to progress it, as the coach told Sky.

“I think it’s difficult for a striker when he doesn’t score goals. But I’ll repeat: we don’t spend much time in the final third of the pitch. We have possession, we’re improving our ball output, but we’re missing that. When we’re consistently in the final third, Gonçalo will score a lot of goals,” he said.

“It’s a team problem, we’re not helping Ramos, but he’s helping us a lot. It’s a process, a journey. And we’re not yet at the point of being so dominant that Ramos spends most of his time in the opponent’s penalty area. We’re still a long way off.”

The Eagles have looked marginally better in other competitions, beating Fulham late last month to book a meeting with Sunderland in the Carabao Cup quarter-finals.

Their Europa League campaign has also been a mixed bag, with one win, two draws and one loss leaving them in 21st place after their first four matches.

Glasner survived a nine-game Premier League winless run in February. But the Austrian, who joined Nottingham Forest in the summer, had credit in the bank, having led Palace to FA Cup and Conference League glory.

Some have suggested Sage – last year’s Ligue 1 manager of the season after guiding Lens to a second-placed finish – was dealt a bad hand, pointing to other areas, including recruitment and injuries, as contributing factors.

But even by his own admission, Palace have lacked consistency, conceding more goals – 24 – than any other top-flight club, while scoring 10, leaving them with the worst goal difference in the division.

#1978. Congo DR vs Sierra Leone - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 10 Nov 2026 23:31, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 23:38

Matchday three of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers sees Congo DR welcome Sierra Leone to Stade des Martyrs on Thursday.

While the hosts have recorded wins from their opening two outings, the visitors make the trip still searching for their first point.

Following a respectable World Cup campaign that ended in a last-32 exit to England, Congo DR began their quest to reach a fourth consecutive major tournament by beating Equatorial Guinea (2-0) and Zimbabwe (2-1) in September.

These results saw Sebastien Desabre’s men open up a three-point advantage at the top of Group E in the AFCON qualifiers, where many have backed them to finish first given their status as the group’s highest-ranked side by FIFA.

However, Les Leopards saw their momentum checked in October’s back-to-back friendly matches against Uganda, suffering a 2-0 defeat before a 1-1 draw three days later, with both matches played in Johannesburg.

Now seeking to replicate their strong start from the previous African qualifying campaign, which saw them win each of their opening four matches, Congo DR face a Sierra Leone side they have beaten in each of the last three encounters, including both meetings in the 2015 qualifiers

Having started the year on a sour note following their AFCON exit to Algeria, Thursday’s hosts will hope to end 2026 on a high.

Victory in their penultimate outing would secure three consecutive competitive wins for the first time since December and deliver a psychological blow to Sierra Leone ahead of their rematch in El Jadida next Tuesday.

Appointed in June to engineer a turnaround, Didier Gomes Da Rosa has endured a difficult start to his Sierra Leone tenure, suffering two defeats from as many matches - the first of which saw his side squander a two-goal lead against Zimbabwe in a 3-2 loss.

That marked a third consecutive loss for the Leone Stars, who now travel to Kinshasa aiming to avoid four straight defeats in all competitions for the first time since June 15; a run that included a 3-1 loss to their upcoming opponents.

Sierra Leone have not featured at an AFCON tournament since 2021, and their hopes of ending that drought have diminished significantly as they sit bottom of Group E ahead of the double-header against Congo DR.

Sierra Leone’s last competitive victory came against Djibouti in October 2025, so confidence is low within the camp. Nonetheless, the West Africans must show resilience over the next few days to keep their already faint AFCON hopes alive.

A positive start on Thursday would provide a much-needed platform for the visitors to build on, but given Congo DR have scored the opening goal in four of their last five matches, Sierra Leone will need to be especially alert early on.

Captain Chancel Mbemba is closing in on his 120th cap for the hosts and continues to extend his record as the nation’s all-time appearances leader.

Despite scoring just once in 27 appearances this season, Malachi Jones has been called up by Sierra Leone and could make his international debut.

#1977. Furious Tottenham set to complain to authorities after Jayden Bogle escapes red card in Leeds' 1-0 win at Elland Road

Published: 13:54 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 14:17 EST, 7 November 2026

Tottenham are to issue a formal complaint over the decision not to show a red card to Leeds defender Jayden Bogle after his challenge on Mathys Tel at Elland Road.

Video replays showed Bogle catch the Spurs forward on the back of his left ankle in the first half of Saturday’s lunchtime kick off but despite a lengthy review by the VAR, referee Jon Brooks was not sent to the pitchside monitor.

Tel came back on but was replaced by Dominic Solanke after 43 minutes and Leeds went on to win the game 1-0 through a Noel Okafor goal.

Spurs, who will lodge their protest with Pro Ref, may cite the red card shown to Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta in the previous Saturday’s clash at the Tottenham Stadium for his foul on Micky van de Ven.

On that occasion, referee Michael Oliver originally gave a yellow card but it was upgraded after a video assistant referee review.

Former Premier League assistant referee Darren Cann told BBC that the Leeds defender was ‘fortunate’ not to be dismissed.

Tel came back on but was replaced by Dominic Solanke after 43 minutes and Leeds went on to win the game 1-0

Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off for this foul on Micky van de Ven in the previous Saturday’s clash

‘Bogle's challenge meets the criteria for serious foul play as he endangers the safety of an opponent,’ Cann said. ‘He can consider himself lucky to still be on the pitch.’

Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi was more critical of his own players afterwards, but did say of the decision: 'I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to the monitor.

'If they didn't take the right decision I don't know. We have to keep the eyes on the performance where can improve.'

The decision will be reviewed by the Key Match Incidents Panel in the coming days. Mateta is serving a three-match suspension after the Football Association rejected Palace's appeal against his red card he received in their 2–0 defeat to Tottenham.

Rio Ferdinand says Mauricio Pochettino is the candidate who ‘jumps off the list’ to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United.

Carrick, 45, looks set to be sacked following United’s disastrous start to the 2026/27 campaign.

Manchester United are 18th in the Premier League going into the November international break, just one point off bottom spot.

Old Trafford bosses are currently reviewing Carrick’s position but a change in the dugout appears to be the most likely outcome.

Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte have all been linked with Manchester United over the past couple of months.

Pochettino has also emerged as a candidate to replace Carrick and Ferdinand has put his support behind the Argentine.

Pochettino, 54, signed an extension to his contract as USA coach after last summer’s World Cup but the deal is believed to contain a release clause.

‘People are talking about Mauricio Pochettino and it looks like he’s at the front of the queue right now,’ Ferdinand said on his YouTube channel.

‘I look at Pochettino and one of his biggest assets is that human element of his management and building confidence with his players. That’s a big part of Manchester United at the moment because we’ve got far too many broken individuals.

#1974. Three outside contenders who could replace Michael Carrick as Man United's next manager

By Ben Sully | 10 Nov 2026 23:44, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 10:47

Manchester United are said to be on the brink of parting ways with head coach Michael Carrick, with the team languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after winning just one of their 10 matches.

While a final decision is yet to be confirmed, rumours are already swirling about who the club could pick as Carrick's replacement should they decide to change head coach over the international break.

USA boss Mauricio Pochettino is reportedly towards the top of the club's managerial shortlist, with his current contract believed to contain a release clause.

Meanwhile, the Red Devils have also been linked with former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe, ex-Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann and the vastly experienced Antonio Conte, who previously managed Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League.

While the aforementioned quartet are believed to be among the main contenders, there may be alternative candidates who are at least on Man United's radar.

With that in mind, Sports Mole highlights three outside picks the Red Devils could consider if they decide to replace Carrick.

According to the latest odds, Kieran McKenna is among the potential contenders for the Man United job, although he is seen as an outsider compared to the likes of Pochettino, Howe, Nagelsmann and Conte.

There is a temptation to say that McKenna ‘knows the club’, but instead of using that tired old cliche, it is perhaps better to say he is someone who will be well-known by many figures at the club, and with that, there is less uncertainty about the way he works as a coach.

McKenna spent a couple of years working as the Under-18 coach at Man United before he was promoted to the role of assistant manager, where he worked with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Jose Mourinho, Ralf Rangnick and Carrick.

The 40-year-old ultimately decided to forge his own path as a manager when he took the top job at Ipswich Town in December 2021, going on to lead the club to back-to-back promotions before suffering Premier League relegation in the 2024-25 campaign.

Ipswich stuck with McKenna and were rewarded with another promotion-winning season, but he ultimately decided against overseeing the club’s latest Premier League campaign, instead opting to take a break from football management.

Considering it has been five months since he made that decision, it is unclear whether McKenna is now ready to jump back into the game, although the chance to manage a club of Man United’s stature would surely be a convincing factor.

There may be a tendency to think he would be a similar appointment to Solskjaer and Carrick due to his previous connections with the club, but he has already built a stronger CV than the aforementioned pair, and his willingness to use width as a means of attack would suit a philosophy that has previously been associated with Man United.

With Fabian Hurzeler and Marco Rose currently impressing at Brighton & Hove Albion and Bournemouth, Man United may want to look to Bundesliga’s exciting coaching talent for their next boss.

Stuttgart boss Sebastian Hoeness is seen as one of the league’s best coaches, even though his side has struggled for consistency this season.

Hoeness got his first taste as a Bundesliga head coach at Hoffenheim, where he oversaw 11th and ninth-placed finishes before taking a year out of management.

In April 2023, the 44-year-old got the call from Stuttgart, who were languishing at the bottom of the table at the time of his appointment.

Hoeness lifted the club out of the automatic relegation spots before he guided them to victory in the relegation/promotion playoff against Hamburg.

Stuttgart’s transformation under Hoeness was there for all to see when the club achieved a runners-up finish in 2023-24, their best league finish in 17 years.

While there was a drop-off in the next Bundesliga campaign, any frustration from a ninth-placed finish was made to feel insignificant by Stuttgart’s triumphant DFB-Pokal, which ended the club’s 28-year wait for glory in the domestic cup.

Champions League qualification followed in the 2025-26 campaign, an achievement that means Hoeness is yet to experience an unsuccessful season at Stuttgart, the sort of consistency that Man United could certainly benefit from.

Hoeness has shown a willingness throughout his coaching career to select a formation that best suits the player profiles in his squad, while still having a clear philosophy to certain aspects of the game, including the willingness for his teams to push full-backs and wing-backs high in a bid to get in good crossing positions.

Out of the three options, Marcelino is the biggest curveball on this list, although he has much more senior management experience than McKenna and Hoeness.

While he may be relatively unknown to an English audience, he has a strong reputation in Spain as a wily operator who tends to command the respect of his players.

Marcelino has managed some of Spain’s biggest clubs, including Sevilla, Valencia and Athletic Club.

The 61-year-old guided Valencia to their first Copa del Rey triumph in 11 years in the 2018-19 season, while he beat Real Madrid for the Spanish Super Cup during his time in charge of Athletic.

However, he perhaps spent his best years in charge of Villarreal, first for a spell from 2013 to 2016 before spending three more years in charge from 2023 to 2026.

In his first stint in charge, Marcelino guided the Yellow Submarine to promotion before achieving three consecutive top-three finishes in La Liga and a run to the Europa League semi-finals in 2015-16.

After returning to the club in November 2023, the experienced coach steered the club to an eighth-placed finish, before leading them to Champions League qualification in back-to-back seasons.

In fact, he guided the club to third spot last season, their best top-flight placing since finishing runners-up in 2007-08, but it proved to be his final campaign in charge after failing to agree terms on a new contract.

Inigo Perez’s struggle to find consistency since taking over the reins at Villarreal has only added to the sense that the club may have made a mistake by allowing him to depart.

However, Villarreal’s potential error may be an opportunity for another club, and while it would be a left-field decision to choose him as Carrick’s replacement, he possesses over 800 games of senior managerial experience, has already coached clubs with demanding fanbases and would not be fazed by the Red Devils’ precarious position in the Premier League relegation zone.

His pragmatism has sometimes been used against him as a criticism, but it may be just what Man United need after shipping 19 goals in 10 Premier League games this season.

Marcelino's keenness to play quickly through the lines and hit teams on the counter may also suit a team that is struggling for confidence in midfield and has players in advanced areas who can race in behind defences.
