#1971. Armenia vs Cyprus - prediction, team news, lineups

By Freddie Cotton | 10 Nov 2026 23:58, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 10:19

Armenia welcome Cyprus to the Vazgen Sargsyan Republican Stadium on Thursday evening for their penultimate League C fixture in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign.

In their previous competition outing, the Collectives played out a goalless draw with Montenegro at the Podgorica City Stadium, while the Blue and Whites claimed a narrow 2-1 victory over Latvia in Nicosia.

After just missing out on promotion to League B in the 2024-25 campaign, finishing second in their group but falling to a thumping 9-1 aggregate defeat against Georgia in the promotion playoff, Armenia will have mixed feelings about how they have started their latest Nations League endeavours.

Despite starting their campaign on the front foot with a 2-0 victory over Latvia in Yerevan, the Collectives have since suffered defeats to Montenegro and Cyprus, although a goalless draw against the former in early October has just about kept Thursday’s hosts in contention for promotion from League C.

With two group matches remaining, Eghishe Melikyan’s men sit third in their respective group, though currently loitering three points below Cyprus in the table, Armenia almost certainly need to claim victory this week if they want any chance of progressing through to a playoff tie.

To do so, the Collectives will certainly have to be better than their recent form suggests too, as despite never before losing a home match against Cyprus, Armenia have claimed victory over the Blue and Whites in just one of their prior eight meetings.

Following a bitterly disappointing World Cup qualifying campaign, winning just one of their six matches to finish fourth in European Group H and sit five points below Romania in the playoff places, Cyprus will be content with how they have bounced back in their latest Nations League efforts.

Although they failed to win either of their first two competition outings, losing to Montenegro in their opening fixture before playing out a stalemate with Latvia, the Blue and Whites have truly kick-started their promotion bid by claiming back-to-back victories and as a result sit in a promising position with just a pair of group matches remaining.

Heading into Thursday’s contest, Apostolos Mantzios’s side sit second in their group with a comfortable cushion over third-placed Armenia, but with Montenegro only three points ahead at the summit, Cyprus still have the opportunity to secure automatic promotion rather than a playoff place, providing plenty of incentive to extend their winning streak through to the end of the campaign.

Having won three of their previous five encounters with Armenia, including a 2-0 victory when the nations met at the GSP Stadium earlier on in the campaign, the Blue and Whites will certainly be confident that they can close down on top spot this week too and craft another chance at winning their place in League B.

Armenia will be without Eduard Spertsyan for Thursday’s contest after the midfielder recently picked up an Achilles tendon injury, while backup goalkeeper Henri Avagyan has also been ruled out.

Sergey Muradyan, Julio Bueno and Sunderland’s Finn Geragusyan round off the hosts’ injury list, though the Collectives are also missing Erik Simonyan, Kamo Hovhannisyan and Vahan Bichakhchyan from the latest squad selection due to a lack of match fitness.

With Henrikh Mkhitaryan retiring from international football in 2022 and Spertsyan out injured, Melikyan’s biggest goal threat on Thursday could well be Tenerife forward Grant-Leon Ranos, who is likely to lead the line for Armenia.

Cyprus are missing both Giannis Satsias and Konstantinos Sotiriou as the pair continue their recovery from muscle issues, while Omonia forward Andronikos Kakoullis remains sidelined with an undisclosed problem.

The Blue and Whites’ only other injury woe is Pafos goalkeeper Charalampos Kyriakidis, who suffered an arm issue in June, though the visitors will also be without Kostas Pileas after the 27-year-old full-back received a red card in last month’s meeting with Armenia.

Having already netted two goals in the current Nations League campaign, Burnley forward Marcus Edwards is undoubtedly Mantzios’s dangerman and is almost certain to start in midfield just behind Ioannis Pittas on Thursday.

Beglaryan; Piloyan, Simonyan, Harutyunyan, Tiknizyan; Iwu, K.Hovhannisyan; Serobyan, Manvelyan, N.Hovhannisyan, Ranos

Fabiano; Konomis, Kyprianou, Panagiotou, Malekkidis; Artymatas, Kastanos; Edwards, Loizou, Georgiou; Pittas

With their form slipping in recent matches and a gap beginning to open up between themselves and the promotion places, it is imperative that Armenia claim all three points against Cyprus if they are to have even the slightest chance of competing in League B when the 2028-29 Nations League campaign gets underway.

However, with the Blue and Whites enjoying a promising run of form and also chasing down Montenegro in the race for automatic promotion, we believe Armenia’s hopes of progressing will run their course on Thursday as the visitors to take all three points in Yerevan.

#1969. RECAP: Nottingham Forest 3-1 Man City - Premier League: Enzo Maresca's men suffer third defeat in a row, as Liam Delap stars to lift his side out of drop zone - at Man United's expense

Oliver Glasner channelled his inner Jose Mourinho when Delap scored Forest's third goal, sprinting down the touchline to celebrate with his players.

In such a precarious job, this victory will mean a lot to him. There's never any guarantee of owner Evangelos Marinakis' patience.

For the first time since 2024, Manchester City have lost three consecutive games in the top fliight.

They're also just the second team in top-flight history to win their first seven games then lose the next three. The previous side to do that were Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05.

I suspect they'll beat Fulham after the international break, but you never know!

Manchester United end a day in the bottom three of the to -flight after having played at least nine games for the first time since November 1986.

Ouch. Thanks to Opta for the stat. They'll be looking to make amends against Aston Villa tomorrow but I don't back them.

Donnarumma had another poor game today, looking flappy. I'm not sure there was much he could have done about the goals, which were all worthy strikes, but conceding three goals won't help a man who has come under increasing scrutiny in recent weeks.

Here's why Maresca stood by him. Do you think it's time for a change?

Why Maresca is sticking with Donnarumma despite Leipzig horror show

JACK GAUGHAN: These are tough times for Donnarumma, a calamitous night in the Champions League adding to the feeling that the past few weeks have not reflected kindly on him.

Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol looked lost today. Enzo Maresca hooked the at half-time after each was at fault for one of the goals. Gvardiol was asleep, giving away the ball for the first, and Guehi just retreated as Delap ran towards goal for the second.

Worrying. Guehi has looked shorn of confidence in recent weeks and this isn't the first time he's been withdrawn at the break.

Today we saw the version of Delap which we know he can be. An absolute bulldozer.

His main flaw is that he typically lacks the finishing. To demonstrate: coming into today, he had scored just two Premier League goals since the start of LAST season. Not a good look.

Well, his finishing was explosive here, as was his running and strength. He's scary when he plays like that.

Manchester United have never been in the relegation zone at this stage of a Premier League season before. Truly abysmal for them.

As for Forest, they can smile after being rewarded for their good performance. They're far from out of the woods, but they did two key things today: score at home, and get Liam Delap's confidence up. Both are critical.

Maresca straight down the tunnel and it didn’t seem as if there was a handshake between him and Oliver Glasner. Dismal night for City but the performance is in keeping with how they are playing. So susceptible on the break and when you’re making this many individual mistakes then the opponents know that they can just wait for them.

Liam Delap has been speaking to Sky Sports.

'It's been coming. We've been performing like that every week but not putting it in the net,' he said.

'We did everything right, got the three points, and are happy going into the international break.

'I just wanted to run and shoot and luckily go there and it went in the net (for first goal).

'Thankfully I put it in the net (for the second).

'We'll have to see it back (Glasner's run down the touchline). Never (seen him run like that).

'We've been deserving this for a long time. Hopefully we can build on it.'

Man City have now lost three times on the spin in the Premier League. Whatever faux title charge they were mounting is collapsing fast at this rate.

The full time whistle blows an Oliver Glasner fist pumps. A HUGE win for Nottingham Forest, one which propels them out of the relegation zone, and plunges Manchester United into it.

#1968. ‘They won’t go away’ - Alan Shearer issues Brighton verdict amid Liverpool and Chelsea title claim

Premier League legend Alan Shearer believes Brighton will push Arsenal all the way in the battle for the title.

The Seagulls are second in the league standings, five points behind leaders Arsenal and one point above third placed Manchester City.

Liverpool are four points adrift of Brighton in fourth place and Xabi Alonso's inconsistent Chelsea are further back in fifth.

The uncertainty surrounding Manchester City and a possible points deduction all adds to the mystery of the title race.

Shearer though has been impressed by Brighton and feels they have the squad and talent to last the distance.

"Brighton could be Arsenal’s main challenge to the title this season," said Shearer to Betfair.

"I think Liverpool are in transition. Chelsea, same thing. They still have plenty of work to do with those football clubs.

"Brighton have been incredible. The football that they're playing, I mean, in Europe too, whether that will hinder them the longer the season goes on I don’t know, but they're managing really well at the minute.

However, Albion’s influential midfielder Pascal Gross dismissed title talk after lat Sunday’s 2-0 win against Brentford at the Amex Stadium.

The 35-year-old German, who has started every match al all competitions for Brighton this term, said: “No, we are not in a title race.

"But we have started the season really well. It’s the beginning of the season.

“You see the Premier League, the margins, you look at the results – we are not getting carried away yet.

“Every game we have to suffer a lot. Sometimes it is momentum. But we are really pleased to head into the international break like this.”

The Seagulls resume action after the international break at Hull City on November 22.

#1966. Boss hopes Lady Luck smiles on Horsham FC as attention turns to FA Trophy tie with Torquay

The Hornets host National League South rivals Torquay United in the FA Trophy second round this Saturday as they look to replicate last season’s run to the quarter-finals.

Horsham have already faced the Gulls this season, drawing 1-1 at Plainmoor on the opening day of the 2026-27 campaign.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Di Paola admitted the Hornets couldn’t have asked for a tougher draw – but the boss hoped a little bit of luck could help Horsham progress.

He told us: “We said when it was drawn it was a tough one but we will approach like we have with every game. We’ll approach it with the right frame of mind.

“I’m desperate to get through. You only have to look at Plymouth Parkway [in the FA Cup] and the draws they’ve had in every round. That’s what you need. I’m not one to blow my own trumpet, but when you do well you do have a bit of luck.

“I’ll always remember the Woking game that got us our first first round [FA Cup appearance in 2021]. They had two or three great chances, Sam Howes made a great save, they missed one at the back post they should have scored, and then with a few minutes to go we scored a free kick that got us into the first round.

“You do need a bit of luck and Plymouth have had a lot of it in terms of draws. They’ve been at home every round – but that’s what you get sometimes. That’s cup football.

“We want to do well in the Trophy like we did last year – it’s good for the finances – but we’re coming up against a team that should make the play-offs comfortably, given the resources they’ve got.

“It’s not an ideal draw but what draw ever is? We would have said Plymouth Parkway was a good draw because they were in the league below, but obviously they were a good side.”

Jimmy Wild is cup-tied for the Trophy tie with Torquay, but the Hornets have no fresh injury concerns.

One player who will no longer feature for Horsham is Archy Taylor, who departed the club on Friday (November 6).

The full-back joined the Hornets ahead of the current season and made a total of 10 appearances.

On Taylor’s departure, Di Paola said: “It’s just unfortunate he’s come up against Lee Harding, who’s one of our best players. He just couldn’t get a foothold in the side.

“With Coxy [George Cox] coming in we have to balance the books, which is perfectly fair. It just got to the point where he wasn’t playing a lot.

“He’s only 22 and he’s probably had two years of setbacks and he just needs to play somewhere and get some football under his belt and get his confidence back. His confidence had gone through the floor because he wasn’t playing, which is common in footballers. He just needs to go and play and enjoy his football somewhere.

“He’s a lovely lad. He saw the writing on the wall and I respect anyone who wants to go and play football. I hate players who are quite happy to sit on the bench or not play.

“Especially younger players, I think money shouldn’t be a factor in your football life when you’re a kid. You should just want to get out and play football while you can because you’re a long time. Fair play to him for wanting to do that. All the best to him.”

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim hopes to welcome three players back during the international break, a report claims.

La Gazzetta dello Sport this morning provided updates on the possible return dates for Strahinja Pavlovic, Fikayo Tomori and Ruben Loftus-Cheek, each of whom missed the win over Genoa due to various muscle issues.

The paper states that Amorim hopes to have all three players back for the match against Frosinone on November 22nd, or during the following week. The break will allow the coach to lighten the work load after a particularly intense period.

The players not called up by their respective national teams will take a few days off and return to training on Monday 16 November. The injured players will continue to use Milanello for their recovery.

#1964. Real Madrid injury news: Jose Mourinho handed Aurelien Tchouameni fitness scare as France release statement

By Ben Sully | 11 Nov 2026 00:16, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 01:52

Real Madrid midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni has withdrawn from Zinedine Zidane's France squad due to injury.

France are preparing to conclude the first phase of the Nations League with an away game against Italy on Thursday and a home meeting with Turkey on Sunday.

Zidane's side are currently sitting top of the standings after collecting 10 points from their opening four games, although they still have work to do to secure a quarter-final spot.

If they are to seal a last eight berth, France will have to do it without the services of Real Madrid's Tchouameni, who has been forced to pull out of the squad with a muscular injury.

In a statement released on Tuesday evening, the French Football Federation said: “Aurelien Tchouameni is once again experiencing discomfort in his right adductor, as he did last summer during the World Cup.

"He has been dealing with this discomfort since arriving at the French National Football Centre in Clairefontaine.

"After taking his medical history into account and holding a conversation just minutes ago with Real Madrid’s medical staff, the French national team’s medical department, in agreement with the player, has decided to release him to his club.

"He will spend tonight with the squad before returning to Madrid tomorrow.”

The FFF also confirmed that no replacement will be called up, leaving Zidane with Eduardo Camavinga, Warren Zaire-Emery, Adrien Rabiot and Lucas Da Cunha as his central midfield options.

Tchouameni, who also missed the last international window, will have to wait until at least March to make his first appearance under Zidane.

Meanwhile, his latest setback will concern Real Madrid, especially as it appears to be a similar issue to the one that forced him to miss the start of the season.

Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho will certainly hope the issue is a minor one, having relied heavily on Tchouameni over the last couple of months.

Los Blancos will return to action against Celta Vigo on November 11 before they face PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League just a few days later.

#1963. Carlton Cole says Man Utd star should have been sold years ago: ‘He’s won the lottery!’

Carlton Cole says Diogo Dalot ‘won the lottery’ when he joined Manchester United and should have been sold years ago.

Dalot is one of the United’s longest-serving players, having made over 250 appearances for the Red Devils since his £19m move from Porto in 2018.

Former Manchester United boss Jose Mourinho hailed Dalot as the ‘best young full-back in Europe’ at the time but the Portugal international has attracted much criticism during his time at Old Trafford.

Dalot has endured a particularly poor couple of weeks, struggling in United’s Champions League win over Roma and Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa in the Premier League.

The 27-year-old was branded ‘atrocious’ after the Roma clash and was booed as he was subbed off by Michael Carrick against Villa.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Ex-England striker Cole is shocked Dalot is still at Manchester United and says the full-back ‘probably can’t believe his luck’.

‘It’s got to be down to Michael Carrick as well,’ Cole said on The Dressing Room podcast when discussing the huge issues at Old Trafford.

‘He’s playing certain personnel in that team that I’m thinking, “how are you even still there?” I’ve said it before but Diogo Dalot, how is he still there?

‘He’s way off it, he is way off it. You can’t depend on him. All he’s thinking about is his next pay check, that’s what’s going through his head.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘He’s not worried about saving the gaffer’s job. He probably can’t believe his luck that he’s there, he’s playing at Old Trafford in front of those brilliant fans in a lovely stadium with all that history.

‘For me, he’s won the lottery. I don’t know how he’s on that pitch. He keeps making the same mistakes and getting caught out, he was at fault last week and he was at fault again at the weekend.’

Manchester United fans cheered when Carrick prepared to sub off Dalot against Aston Villa and then booed as he made his way off the pitch.

Asked about that reaction after the game, Carrick said: ‘We’ve got to be careful with that, I think. I understand the frustration. I understand the disappointment of the supporters, so I get it.

‘We’re all frustrated. We’re all disappointed. And the players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that.

‘Diogo gives absolutely everything. He’s played in different positions. He’s played left-back. He’s played really well at times. He gives a penalty away today. That’s, you know… he knows that.

‘Maybe he can do a little bit better. Alright, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake. But he cares an awful lot, and he’s given everything.

‘So I like what he brings to the team. I like what he brings to the group. I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we’ve got.

‘Picking the team and who plays the next game, that’s a whole different decision. But it’s a whole different game that we’ve got to look forward to now.’

An eighth league game without a win leaves Manchester United 18th in the Premier League going into the November international break.

A dismal start to the 2026/27 campaign looks set to cost Carrick his job at Old Trafford, with Eddie Howe the current frontrunner to take over.

#1962. Liverpool news: Virgil van Dijk "not in any panic" as Reds captain issues update on contract situation

By Ben Sully | 11 Nov 2026 00:56, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 01:05

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk insists he is "not in any panic" over his contract situation at Anfield.

The Netherlands international has been one of Liverpool's star players since he arrived from Southampton in the summer of 2018.

Van Dijk has made 389 appearances for the Reds, helping the club win multiple pieces of silverware, including two Premier League titles and a Champions League crown.

While he may not be at the age of 35, Van Dijk continues to play a prominent role for the Merseyside club, having started 14 of the club's 16 competitive matches this season.

As it stands, it is unclear if this is the final season of his successful Liverpool career, with his current deal set to expire at the end of the campaign.

Van Dijk has now issued an update on his contract situation, explaining that he is not stressing about his uncertain Anfield future.

“I want to keep playing and continue what I’m doing, so let’s see what the season brings,” Van Dijk told reporters.

“I’ve had an amazing time already so far. If that will be extended, that’s the case.

"If not, then I will go somewhere else. There’s nothing to report at the moment but that doesn’t mean that there’s any stress or anything.

“I feel good but it’s not about me at the moment. I’m not in any panic whatsoever.”

With Van Dijk set to turn 36 next summer, there will be an obvious temptation to look to the long-term future and sign a younger defender who could fill Van Dijk's boots for years to come.

However, the Dutchman is still continuing to perform at a high level and has formed a strong central defensive partnership with Jeremy Jacquet this term.

The defender also plays a crucial role as captain, and his leadership will certainly be tough to replace when the time comes for him to leave Anfield.

With that in mind, the Reds should do their utmost to keep Van Dijk for at least another season, although it remains to be seen whether the player himself will look to sign a new deal or take the decision to leave while he is still performing at a high level.

In the short term, Van Dijk's current focus will be on returning to full fitness after withdrawing from Xavi's Netherlands squad with a minor issue.

#1960. Martin Zubimendi responds to Chelsea transfer speculation and reveals Mikel Arteta warning

Martin Zubimend has revealed he was warned he would face a fight to maintain his status as a regular starter at Arsenal this season, but insists he hasn’t given up hope of winning back his place.

The Spain international joined the Gunners 18 months ago following a £60million move from Real Sociedad.

Zubimendi had come close to signing for Liverpool a year earlier, but was convinced to snub the Reds’ interest and delay a move to England, with Mikel Arteta outlining his determination to make him a key component of his midfield rebuild.

The 27-year-old’s decision to move to the north London club initially looked an inspired one as he played almost every game over the course of the first two thirds of a campaign that ultimately ended in glory.

Fatigue, however, eventually caught up with Zubimendi and his place was effectively taken by teenager Myles Lewis-Skelly during the run-in and he has been reduced to a bit-part role ever since.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Arsenal’s decision to sanction the signing of Bruno Guimaraes has only served to further heighten the intense competition for places and, as a result, Zubimendi is yet to start a Premier League game this season.

That lack of game time has sparked intense speculation that a January move could be on the cards for the World Cup winner.

Chelsea, who are in the market for a midfielder and whose manager, Xabi Alonso, attempted to sign Zubimendi during his brief stint in charge of Real Madrid, are said to be considering renewing interest having made tentative enquiries during the summer.

Atletico Madrid, meanwhile, have been positioned as the frontrunners, with Diego Simeone said to be dreaming of signing the Arsenal star with reports in Spain going as far as saying that a deal is close.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Responding to a whirlwind of rumours, Zubimendi told Marca: ‘To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press too. I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumors can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish.

‘Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close, but not at all.

‘Often a news story comes out and it seems that if it doesn’t come true, it’s quickly forgotten and nothing happens. I’m learning how this world works and getting used to it, but sometimes I could avoid a lot of the messages I receive because of this kind of news.’

Asked whether his current predicament has come as a surprise, Zubimendi revealed Arteta had been totally transparent at the season’s outset and outlined the role he envisaged for a player he fought so hard to sign.

He said:  ‘I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season. As he does with all the players, he explained the plan to me.

‘He warned me that there were new signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it.

‘I understand because, for me, we’re among the five best teams in Europe. There are some fantastic players. New signings have arrived in my position, and there were already some very good players. I’m also part of that competition that makes it so difficult to get playing time.’

He added:  ‘I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation. It’s something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too.

‘Besides, it’s in moments like these that you need the people around you the most, and they’re there for you.

‘I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side. I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very quickly.’

#1959. Man United chiefs considering 'one option' that could save Michael Carrick from sack

By Ben Sully | 11 Nov 2026 01:35, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 01:48

Manchester United have reportedly considered new coaching support as a potential option should they decide against sacking Michael Carrick.

The Man United boss appears to be on the brink of the sack after overseeing one win in 10 Premier League games this season (D5, L4).

While his side staged a late fightback to salvage a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, the Red Devils are in a precarious position in the Premier League drop zone, with one point separating them from safety.

Man United's director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada will hold a crucial meeting with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday.

Carrick's future will be the main topic of discussion, with Wilcox and Berrada expected to recommend a change of head coach.

As a result, the writing appears to be on the wall for Carrick, although BBC Sport claims there is one option that could offer the 45-year-old a lifeline.

Instead of sacking their current head coach, Man United's decision-makers could look to add coaching staff to Carrick's backroom team.

Bayern Munich assistant Aaron Danks is believed to be one option after being linked with a potential role on Carrick's support staff in the summer.

Danks previously worked with Carrick at Middlesbrough, but there is surely considerable doubt as to whether he would leave Bayern at this time.

The 43-year-old has recently demonstrated his importance to Bayern after taking charge of first-team duties for the last five games in the absence of Vincent Kompany due to health reasons.

Having spent over two years working alongside Kompany in Germany, there is little reason to suggest he would consider leaving during the season, especially as Bayern have aspirations of challenging on all fronts, including the Champions League.

In truth, the thought of even offering additional coaching support to Carrick suggests that confidence has already been lost in the head coach.

That is why the most likely outcome is for Carrick to depart and Man United to appoint a successor ahead of their Premier League clash against Liverpool on November 22.

Pietro Terracciano, Matteo Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Alexis Saelemaekers, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Samuel Chukwueze and Strahinja Pavlovic were all out for the match at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris, with the Serbian centre-back being the latest to enter the treatment room.

In today’s edition of Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews), Ordine analysed Milan’s win at the Marassi. He spoke about how the injury situation has forced Amorim to make certain choices, ones that lay everything bare in view of a potentially important winter transfer window.

#1957. Commentators haven't the foggiest idea what's going on: Thick mist ruins FA Cup clash for TV viewers - and fans use phone torches to see the action!

Published: 16:25 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 16:27 EST, 7 November 2026

'Peak FA Cup', was the verdict from TV viewers watching (or trying to watch) the clash between Notts County and Altrincham as thick fog obscured the action.

Those tuning in on TNT Sports were baffled by what was actually happening in the game when the mist descended at Moss Lane.

Commentators saw the funny side, with Adam Summerton chuckling, saying: 'Your guess is as good as mine at the minute,' when asked by his partner what was going on.

As the match progressed, the foggy conditions only worsened and it became difficult for the players to see far in front of them, let alone those trying to spectate in the ground and at home.

Even though the conditions appeared to simply be deep fog, one local claimed it was smoke from local firework parties causing the white-out.

They wrote: 'It is smoke from the bonfire night fireworks and bonfires. I live round the corner, it is literally just smoke. All you can smell in the air is smoke.'

The fog is closing in at Moss Lane! 🌫️Conditions are getting tricky for Altrincham and Notts County 👀📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/gTM9e3KA2w

Fog descended on the FA Cup clash between Altrincham and Notts County and TV viewers could hardly tell what was going on

Fans pulled out the torches on their phones in a light-hearted bid to see more of the action

Despite the lack of quality action for fans to watch at Moss Lane, plenty of them saw the funny side and even took out their phone torches in unison to try and cut through the gloom.

Those at home poked fun at the scene, with one posting: 'Can you ask the ref that if it goes to pens they bring the goal closer to the cameras so we can watch them?'

Another wrote: 'Where's the orange ball? I miss those days!'

Not everyone could see the humour in the situation, with one user on X writing: 'I'm sorry but this is ridiculous it should be abandoned. You could be miles offside.'

The game itself went to penalties, which caused further problems for the commentators, who had to largely base their reactions on the crowd directly behind the goal.

Ultimately, Notts County survived a scare from the non-league outfit and won 3-2 in the shootout.

Rosaire Longelo netted the final spot-kick to fire the Magpies into the second round of the FA Cup.

They'd had to fight back from 2-1 down in normal time after Lucas Weaver and then Lewis Banks put Altrincham in front.

Callum Roberts scored to make it 2-2 and neither side could find a winner in extra-time, meaning an already memorable game was settled in a fitting and dramatic fashion.

#1956. Manchester United finalising deal to appoint Michael Carrick’s replacement

Manchester United are close to rubber stamping a deal to appoint Michael Carrick’s successor ahead of making a final decision on the future of their current head coach.

The Red Devils are languishing in the relegation zone after Sunday’s chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa which is expected to represent Carrick’s final game at the helm, despite an injury-time comeback which yielded an unlikely point.

Carrick currently remains in limbo and attended United’s training ground on Wednesday morning with club executives set to discuss his future at a meeting in Monaco.

The 45-year-old was photographed driving into the club’s Carrington base this morning, but his fate is set to be determined at a meeting 800 miles away, where co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe will confer with United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

According to the Athletic, United’s key decision makers held talks on Tuesday and settled on Mauricio Pochettino as the candidate best qualified to lead the club out of the almost unprecedented mess it finds itself in.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager signed a contract with US Soccer through to 2030 just three months ago, and is currently preparing the American national side for CONCACAF Nations League matches against Haiti in the November international break.

The former Argentina international has held talks with United in the past and is keen on the job this time, but hefty compensation would be due to US Soccer.

United are understood to have been in contact with Pochettino’s representatives and although personal terms are unlikely to be an issue, the 54-year-old’s exit clause of £7.4million would need to be paid in full.

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery is admired, while ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and former Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann were linked a fortnight ago when United seriously considered replacing Carrick.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

A 4-1 Champions League loss at Como and 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth left the head coach’s job hanging by a thread, but the club decided to give him the opportunity to turn the situation around.

Carrick’s side subsequently lost 2-0 at Chelsea, where they were unable to take their chances and saw Lisandro Martinez sent off, before last Tuesday’s thrilling 3-2 Champions League comeback win against Roma.

A scarcely believable 4-4 draw against followed on Sunday, after which the head coach stressed he would not walk away.

‘It’s been a right mixed week or two or three, really, if you’re looking at the events,’ Carrick said. ‘But I’m pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there.

‘Obviously some of the boys will be flying off around the world and different things, and the group will be split for 10 days or so.

‘But as a normal international week is, you know, we’ll have some training. We’ll have one or two days off, but not too much. But we’ll train, and we’ll get ready for the next game.’

United return to action with a Premier League trip to rivals Liverpool on November 22.

Bournemouth have ruled out a transfer move for rumoured Arsenal target Eli Junior Kroupi this January.

Arsenal scoured the market for attacking reinforcements in the summer transfer window, with Mikel Arteta keen to add firepower to his title-winning frontline.

Christos Tzolis was signed for a fee of £34million from Club Brugge to help fill the void left by the departure of both Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli – and the Greece international has gone on to enjoy an encouraging start to life in north London.

However, it was clear the Premier League champions had ideally intended to bring in another proven talent in this area of the pitch after the club were gazumped by Chelsea in the race for Morgan Rogers.

According to talkSPORT, Arsenal are ready to reenter the transfer market to land a top-class attacker this winter and have a number of high-profile names on their shortlist of possible solutions.

Asked if he’d been congratulated by any thankful Arsenal players at the time, he told Stadium Astro: ‘Yes I have received many messages but I tell myself that I didn’t do this for Arsenal.

‘It doesn’t change anything, I just wanted to help my team.’

When asked about his goals and ambitions for the future, Kroupi replied: ‘Perform with my team and perform also in Europe also because it is very beautiful to be in Europe but you have to perform to play there.’

#1953. A nugget of pure quality - how Kieran Morgan caught the eye on a chill night for Bradford City

The QPR loan midfielder was involved in much of the good work that the Bantams produced in their final EFL Trophy northern group game against White Rose rivals York City - with goals from Antoni Sarcevic, Stephen Humphrys, Will Swan and Nick Powell seeing the hosts emphatically confirm top spot and a home tie in the knock-out phases.

One moment stood out in the first half when Morgan showed sumptuous technique to strike a shot with the outside of his foot which clipped the post.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

And it arrived on the back of an encouraging display in the club's FA Cup blitzing of Marine.

City may have gorged on 11 goals in two resounding Valley Parade cup wins to start getting the Huddersfield Town derby loss out of their system and answer talk that they are goal-shy, but Morgan's poise in the middle was among the key elements.

Boss Michael Duff, who handed debuts to the impressive Zac Hadi, Leeroy Gomes, Gabe Holt and Oliver Hewitt - with Harry Ibbitson making his home bow - said: "It takes time and opportunity. And when the team's been going so well, it's tough to get those opportunities. So all he can do is, when he gets opportunities, do what he's done in the last two games.

"I think he's been very, very good in both games.

"He's a good player. Forty to fifty Championship games, you don't do that by accident.

"The press is a little bit unique here, so it's slightly different.

"So it takes a bit of probably getting used to, in terms of one minute you're in that 10 position and then you've got to be a six. And it takes time and training. And we've not had loads of time to train.

"We've had four (proper) training sessions (since Duff joined). So it's been tough to get into any sort of rhythm anyway."

The one sour note from a rewarding night came with Duff's post-match confirmation that Bobby Pointon’s knee injury sustained at the weekend has sidelined him for a minimum of eight weeks.

Cameron Dawson (calf), George Lapslie (hamstring) are set to be out for up to four weeks, but Josh Neufville should be available for the home derby with Doncaster Rovers on November 21.

Despite a 4-0 loss, York - already eliminated from the Trophy and still seeking their maiden away win on their return to the EFL - performed well for the opening hour before being blown away.

Minstermen chief Scott Lindsey felt the scoreline was cruel, with some justification.

Lindsey, who changed his entire starting line-up from last weekend, said: "It wasn't a 4-0 game for me and I was really pleased with lots of it, to be fair.

"We had two young 18-year-old's start the game and I think we finished with three 18-year-old's and a 17-year-old. I'm really proud of those boys.

"Obviously, there were some older pros who needed some much-needed minutes.

"All in all, it was a good exercise,” added Lindsey.

"It was always going to be hard when their teamsheet came in, but I actually relished that and thought it would be a good test.

"There were lots to be really pleased about, but games are won and lost in both boxes.

"We had some good chances, we just didn't put them away and they did."

#1952. New Zealand vs India - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 11 Nov 2026 02:09, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 05:00

India are set for a tough test on Thursday, when they travel to Auckland's Go Media Stadium for an international friendly against New Zealand, marking their first-ever visit to the country.

The All Whites are hoping to bounce back from defeat last time out, while the Blue Tigers are looking to follow the winning example set by their alternative squad at the SAFF Championship.

Darren Bazeley's New Zealand followed up their group-stage elimination from World Cup 2026 with a three-game unbeaten run, drawing 2-2 with Palestine before triumphing 3-0 against China and on penalties against Panama during the last international break.

However, the All Whites' streak came to an end on October 5, when they were downed 2-1 by Japan in the final of the friendly Kirin Cup.

Captain Chris Wood - the nation's record scorer and appearance holder - assisted Ben Old's equaliser that day, but he was unable to respond when Ritsu Doan netted the winner for the Samurai Blue four minutes after his second-half substitution.

Looking ahead to Thursday, the hosts have never lost to India, most recently running out 2-1 winners in the friendly AIFF Intercontinental Cup in June 2018.

However, this week's clash will be just the second time they have faced the visitors this century, and only the third meeting between the sides throughout history, after first locking horns during a goalless draw in the 1981 edition of the Merdeka Tournament.

New Zealand (ranked 88th) are the favourites to come out on top due to their 50-superior placement in FIFA's ranking system, though fans may still be cautious considering that Bazeley's team have lost two of their last three matches on home turf.

Meanwhile, Khalid Jamil's India arrive as underdogs but are keen to test their mettle in a pair of fixtures against an opponent who qualified for the World Cup.

Thursday's friendly in Auckland and Sunday's follow up in Christchurch come as part of a celebration marking 100 years of sporting connection between the nations, and the Blue Tigers' manager called for fans to join them on matchday in his press conference.

“I know there are many Indian fans here in New Zealand - I would request them to come to the stadium and support the team. Their support is important for us, and we will try to give our best on the pitch,” said Jamil.

Another challenge facing the visitors is the fact they are split across two squads, one that is set to take part in these friendlies and another that is currently contesting the 2026 SAFF Championship, the latter of which beat Pakistan 3-2 on November 5.

Beyond that victory by their alternative side, India are heading into this clash on the back of a seven-game winless run in friendlies, including a 6-1 thrashing by Uruguay and a 4-0 hammering by Brazil last month.

New Zealand International Friendlies form:

New Zealand are without right-back Callan Elliot through injury, but the versatile Bill Tuiloma could feature in his absence, joining Nando Pijnaker, Tyler Bindon and James McGarry in defence.

At the opposite end of the pitch, Chris Wood looks set to lead the line, supported from out wide by Dundee United's Jesse Randall and 20-year-old Nathan Walker of Wellington Phoenix, who could make his All Whites debut.

As for India, they have left experienced goalkeeper Gurpreet Singh Sandhu out of the squad, while centre-back Anwar Ali is sidelined due to a hamstring injury.

With that in mind, Vishal Kaith is likely to start between the sticks on Thursday, shielded by a pairing of Bijoy Varghese and Mehtab Singh.

The Blue Tigers are also without midfielder Lalengmawia Ralte, who is known as Apuia, though Anirudh Thapa could be joined by Lalrinliana Hnamte in the visitors' double pivot.

Paulsen; Tuiloma, Pijnaker, Bindon, McGarry; Rufer; Randall, Garbett, Bayliss, Walker; Wood

Kaith; Singh Tekcham, Varghese, Me Singh, Mishra; Hnamte, Thapa; Ma Singh, Williams, Kuruniyan; Lalhlansanga

New Zealand are the overwhelming favourites despite featuring a number of young players in their squad, and they will be hoping to deliver a strong showing on home soil.

India will arrive knowing that they are likely to be on the losing side, but that underdog status could inspire them to find the back of the net at least once on Thursday.

#1951. Danny Murphy tells Liverpool to explore transfer move for £33m Man Utd target

Danny Murphy has urged Liverpool to strongly consider a transfer move for Barcelona misfit Alejandro Balde this winter.

Liverpool invested heavily in the summer with a view to giving Andoni Iraola the best possible chance in the hot seat following Arne Slot’s dismissal as manager.

It saw Jeremy Jacquet, Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz all added to Iraola’s squad for a combined fee of around £200million – and the trio have gone on to enjoy encouraging starts to life at Anfield.

With the Reds having dropped points in five of their opening ten matches of the Premier League campaign, though, attentions have quickly turned to the January transfer window as an opportunity to further strengthen.

Milos Kerkez has blown hot and cold since joining Liverpool for a fee of £40million from Bournemouth 18 months ago and rumours have been circulating that the club could reenter the transfer market for a new left-back.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The Merseyside giants have been credited with a strong interest in Juventus’ Andrea Cambiaso and Santos’ Vinicius Lira in recent days, with Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas both yet to fully convince fans that they could eventually fill the shoes left by Andy Robertson.

But according to Murphy, ‘super talent’ Balde could be the ideal signing for Liverpool given the out-of-favour Spaniard is already used to the expectations that come with playing for a ‘huge football club’.

Balde has made just three substitute appearances for Barca in La Liga this term and Manchester United have also been named as a potential escape route for the £33m-rated defender at the halfway point of the season.

‘I think Liverpool will be looking for a left-back but it’s hard because I don’t know Kerkez personally, I know he’s trying really hard and you can see it in his energy that he cares, and that’s a great start,’ the ex-Liverpool and England midfielder told Betarades.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘He cares for the shirt and he’s working really hard to try and make it happen.

‘I think Balde could be great for Liverpool because he’s a super talent and he’s also got that experience of being at a huge football club with that expectation.

‘Balde’s a really good player. There’s lots of good players out there and Liverpool will be scouring the world.’

Murphy believes it could be time for Liverpool to look for ‘more established’ and ‘ready-made players’ after prioritising youth in recent transfer windows.

‘I think the most important thing is trying to bring somebody in who doesn’t make you guess whether he can deal with the pressure of a big club,’ he added.

‘It’s a delicate balance because Liverpool for years were very good at taking diamonds in from the rough, if you like. Someone like [Philippe] Coutinho, like [Andy] Robertson, like [Sadio] Mane even from Southampton. [Roberto] Firmino was about £20m.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘Liverpool took those diamonds in the rough and moulded them into these superstars, and then when we’ve tried to go and spend massive money on these already made stars, it’s not quite worked.

‘I still think there are times, especially in defensive areas where you really do want ready-made players. Especially when you’re struggling.

‘I think Liverpool have got enough young players now who need to grow. I think now there’s an argument to have a few more players who are maybe a bit more established.’

Murphy has some sympathy for Kerkez but feels the Hungary international needs to get his head down and work on his composure if he is to make a success of his time at Liverpool.

‘He just lacks composure and quality in the final third when he gets there. Too often his final pass or his cross isn’t good enough,’ he continued.

‘He doesn’t have the composure of an Andy Robertson, and to be fair to him, you are filling the boots of arguably one of the best left-backs Liverpool’s ever had.”

‘I think the lack of quality at times is due to the fact he’s very fast. He’s very much 100 miles an hour. I’m surprised they’re not working with him more to slow him down in those areas and to just calm himself.

‘Now it wouldn’t be as bad if he was brilliant defensively, but he’s struggling defensively as well. His positional play is sometimes a bit off, he’s a bit erratic in terms of diving in or getting beat.

‘He likes jumping into people. It’s a dilemma for Liverpool, and I think one that they’ll definitely be looking at and trying to address, because not every signing works out.’

On Kerkez, Murphy went on: ‘I was somebody who saw him that year at Bournemouth and thought he looked like a terrific young player.

‘But the one thing that people don’t understand and it’s only when you’ve been in that position you can empathise with going from playing in one environment to being in the intense, magnified world of Liverpool Football Club.

‘Every game, every minute, every mistake is analysed by the fans, by the press, by the worldwide audience, and I think that expectation, and that pressure is a bit much for him.’

#1949. Chelsea named as ‘best placed’ to sign £60m Arsenal star in January transfer window

Chelsea are leading the race ahead of Atletico Madrid to sign Martin Zubimendi in the January transfer window, according to reports in Spain.

Zubimendi joined Arsenal in a £60 million deal from Real Sociedad last year and played an integral role in his first season at the club as Mikel Arteta’s side won the Premier League and reached the Champions League final.

So far this season, Zubimendi is yet to start in 10 Premier League games and is facing increased competition for a place in midfield following Arsenal’s decision to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United in the summer.

Both Chelsea and Atletico Madrid have been linked with a move for Zubimendi, and his Spain teammate, Alex Baena, said this week that the Arsenal midfielder would be a ‘great addition’ to the Spanish club.

However, Spanish reporter Antonio Ruiz told El Partidazo de COPE on Tuesday night that Atletico have ruled themselves out of the race to sign Zubimendi in January.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘Reliable sources of Atletico Madrid have denied it and negotiations have been ruled out, nor is there any intention of signing Zubimendi in January,’ Ruiz said.

‘Neither a negotiation or an intention, that was literally the answer from the club.

‘There was a consideration a long time ago about the possibility of Julian Alvarez being involved in a swap deal with Zubimendi. The club [Atletico] say they haven’t considered it.

‘I also contacted someone in Zubimendi’s entourage and he is very calm. I asked what happens if he left Arsenal, the best-placed team would be Chelsea with Xabi Alonso, not Atletico Madrid.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘In the event that he does decide to leave, the option that fits most is Chelsea.’

In an interview with Marca this week, Zubimendi insisted he is ‘calm’ about his lack of playing time at Arsenal and revealed he was warned by Mikel Arteta about the competition in midfield this season.

‘I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season. As he does with all the players, he explained the plan to me,’ Zubimendi said.

‘He warned me that there were new signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it.

‘I understand because, for me, we’re among the five best teams in Europe. There are some fantastic players. New signings have arrived in my position, and there were already some very good players. I’m also part of that competition that makes it so difficult to get playing time.

‘I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation. It’s something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too.

‘Besides, it’s in moments like these that you need the people around you the most, and they’re there for you.

‘I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side. I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very quickly.’

#1948. Guatemala vs Canada - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 11 Nov 2026 02:46

Making their first appearance in the quarter-finals of the CONCACAF Nations League, Guatemala will host Canada in the opening leg of that tie on Friday at Estadio El Trebol in Guatemala City.

A 1-0 win over Suriname helped the Guatemalans top Group B with seven points, while Canada are one of the top four ranked teams in CONCACAF, earning a bye into the knockout stage as a result.

It was a roller coaster of a group stage for Guatemala, but fortunately for them it ended with the Central Americans at the top.

Luis Fernando Tena’s men opened that phase by conceding an injury-time goal in a defeat to Jamaica (3-2) but ended it with an stoppage-time winner versus Suriname.

That victory vaulted them into the Nations League knockout stage for the first time, scoring nine goals along the way, the joint-most for them ever in the League A group phase.

Unfortunately though it came at a cost as the coach will be missing some players for this match due to the post-match altercations in that outing.

Since their heartbreaking defeat on matchday one to the Jamaicans, Guatemala have collected a clean sheet in their last three Nations League affairs, having conceded a combined 14 goals this year before this tournament began.

In their six previous League A encounters at home, this team have yet to lose, while conceding a mere two goals overall during that stretch.

Los Chapines can stretch their unbeaten run against Canada to three matches across all competitions, eliminating them on penalties in the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup quarter-finals.

Following their historic run to the last 16 of the World Cup last summer, the Canadians had a solid fall international window.

Jesse Marsch’s men won two of their three friendlies in that window, collecting two clean sheets along the way.

On Friday, they will hope to avoid consecutive international defeats for the first time since the 2024 Copa America, after losing their last international outing to the USA (1-0).

The Canucks boast a 100% away record in the quarter-finals of this tournament, winning at Jamaica in 2023 (2-1) and blanking Suriname on the road a year later (1-0).

They have won their last four internationals when netting the opening goal and have never lost a knockout match in this competition as the visiting team.

Friday will be their second Nations League match on Central American soil, with Les Rouges losing the previous one in the group stage at Honduras in 2022 (2-1).

Because of a post-match confrontation against Suriname, Jonathan Franco and Carlos Estrada will be suspended for three matches, while Oscar Santis is out due to a hamstring strain.

Matt Evans netted in the 96th minute to earn them a place in the knockout stage of this competition, his first goal on the international stage, and Nicholas Hagen collected two clean sheets in the group phase.

Canadian captain Alphonso Davies is reportedly ready to play according to Marsch, though Jonathan Osorio and Jacob Shaffelburg withdrew with injuries, while Cyle Larin was not selected because of back irritation.

Davies can move into a tie for ninth in all-time international goals Friday, while Richie Laryea will draw even with Paul Stalteri for sixth in all-time caps with his next one.

Hagen; Herrera, Yanes, Samayoa, Morales; Lopez, Castellanos, Rosales, Escobar, Rubin, Lom

Crepeau; Laryea, De Fougeroles, Ivanisevic, Davies; Buchanan, Saliba, Choiniere, Millar; J. David, Oluwaseyi

Even with Davies back, the environment in Guatemala will be difficult for the visitors to navigate, and we expect the Central Americans’ suffocating defence to limit the scoring chances for Canada.

#1947. Charlie wins battle of the Savages! Son scores in 5-0 FA Cup hammering of dad Robbie's Peterborough United - as manager appears to try and supress smile

Published: 17:03 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 17:26 EST, 7 November 2026

Charlie Savage came out on top in the FA Cup's Battle of the Savages with a goal against his dad Robbie's new team, Peterborough United.

Already two goals up thanks to strikes by Daniel Kyerewaa and Jack Marriott, Reading made a place in round two virtually secure when Robbie's son Charlie added a third in first-half stoppage time.

The midfielder, 23, latched on to a loose ball on the edge of the Peterborough area and fired home, with the aid of a slight deflection, before racing off towards the visiting fans and celebrating with a knee slide.

Dad Robbie, who took over as Posh boss last month after his stint at Forest Green Rovers, looked initially frustrated at his team's defending but you almost sensed a smile given the identity of the goalscorer.

'Charlie Savage's goal is all about him seeing the danger, holding his run, letting it run across his body and finishing,' said former Reading midfielder Steve Sidwell on BBC Sport. 'Reading are deservedly in charge of the game, and Savage has been superb.'

Former Leicester midfielder and Wales international Robbie had feared as much in an exclusive interview with the Daily Mail before the first-round tie.

Charlie Savage scores against his dad Robbie’s side! 😳Reading make it 3-0 at Peterborough! 🔥📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/RmMzxfNIzE

'Charlie Savege's goal is all about him seeing the danger, holding his run, letting it run across his body and finishing,' said former Reading midfielder Steve Sidwell

Savage Jnr celebrates with a knee slide that his dad would have been proud of

Charlie takes advice from the Reading bench as his father Robbie (centre) looks on

'It's going to be horrible,' he had said. 'Every time I watch my sons play, I'm anxious. I'm nervous. I want them to do well. If they give the ball away and the other team attack, I've got butterflies thinking, "Please don't score".

That particular wish took on a new meaning as his lad lined up to shoot with his left foot to strengthen Reading's vice-like grip on the tie.

Like his dad, Charlie came through Manchester United's youth ranks and made one first-team appearance, as a substitute at the age of 18 against Young Boys in the Champions League. It was an unforgettable night for Robbie, who was on co-commentary duty with a lump in his throat.

Much the same applied on Saturday night, though this time there were mixed emotions in the Savage household.

It got worse, much worse, as Jamie Reid netted twice in the second half to make it 5-0 to the visitors.

Peterborough can now focus on improving their position from third bottom of League One, while Reading may wish to put thoughts of Wembley to one side as they set their sights on a promotion push.

#1945. Real Madrid transfer news: Endrick prepares exit with one club favourites, and it's not Arsenal

By Axel Clody | 11 Nov 2026 06:57, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 06:57

Endrick is expected to leave Real Madrid again in the January transfer window. A Champions League club has been installed as favourites to land him.

Seven matches played, a single start, one goal and one assist: that is Endrick’s statistical record in the start of this season at Real Madrid.

After a successful loan at Lyon in the second half of last season, the Brazilian striker returned to Real Madrid, but the competition in attack is too great. A departure seems increasingly likely.

Asked about his future on Tuesday, Endrick made no secret of his intention to play more. ‘I don’t know what will happen in January’ - he conceded, before adding: ‘I just want to play, I want to be happy, help my teammates, score goals, provide assists. What happened to me at Lyon, for example, was one of the best things that happened to me in my life, the moment I was happiest, without a doubt.’

According to AS, the former Palmeiras player feels good at Real Madrid and gets on well with Jose Mourinho, but he needs to leave to continue his progress. ‘The situation would have to change radically for Endrick not to leave in January’, says the Spanish newspaper.

Currently, less than two months before the January transfer window opens, the Real Madrid player is preparing his departure and looking for a new destination.

A rebound like the one offered by Lyon last winter is being sought, where he would have guaranteed playing time and the chance to play European matches.

Roma are interested in Endrick’s profile, but Sporting represent a formidable competitor in this race. The Portuguese club have already positioned themselves to sign the Brazilian in the second half of the season.

Paulo Fonseca, who had him under his orders at Lyon, has asked for his recruitment.

Sporting have everything of the ‘ideal place’ for the 20-year-old, according to AS.

The Portuguese club are playing in the Champions League and currently sit 10th in the league phase, and are therefore well placed to reach the knockout stages. In Lisbon, Endrick would find a club where he knows the manager, with whom he has already performed, and where he also speaks the language.

It should be noted that the striker, who is also on Arsenal’s shortlist, has not yet made a decision and has not ruled out leaving on a permanent transfer, which would guarantee Real Madrid retained control over his future, either through a buy-back clause or the sale of part of his rights.

Jamie Redknapp says Andrey Santos is ‘not a Manchester United player’ and claims whoever was responsible for his signing ‘deserves the sack’.

Desperate for midfield reinforcements over the summer, United spent £50m to sign Brazil international Santos from Premier League rivals Chelsea.

Manchester United made midfield targets their priority after Casemiro left Old Trafford and Manuel Ugarte suffered a serious injury at the World Cup.

Carlos Baleba and Youri Tielemans joined Michael Carrick’s squad on top of Santos but all three midfielders have made inauspicious starts to their United careers.

Redknapp doubts the 22-year-old Brazilian is at the level required to play for United and says bringing him to the club was a ‘sackable offence’ by those in charge at Old Trafford.

‘Can I throw one player at you? And this is no disrespect to the boy, because he’s not a bad player, but whoever brought in Andrey Santos, that for me is a sackable offence,’ Redknapp said on The Overlap Daily, sponsored by Sky Vegas.

According to Foot Mercato journalist Santi Aouna, super-agent Pini Zahavi is representing Conte in discussions over the Red Devils job.

The 57-year-old is among the candidates being considered by the United hierarchy, with Zahavi potentially helping to position him for an appointment.

It's believed that Conte remains on the shortlist alongside Pochettino, although there are still some doubts within the club about whether the former Inter Milan, Chelsea and Spurs manager is the right fit.

However, with Carrick expected to depart in the coming days barring an unexpected development, United could soon need to make a decisive move.

Conte boasts an impressive managerial CV, having won six domestic league titles during his career, including the Premier League with Chelsea and Serie A with both Juventus and Inter Milan.

His reputation for demanding intensity, discipline and high standards could appeal to a club looking for a significant change in direction.

There is an argument that Conte's forceful personality is exactly what United need after another period of instability.

He has a proven ability to transform teams quickly, while his structured tactical approach and preference for physically demanding football could help address some of the weaknesses in United's current side.

Harry Kane, who worked under Conte at Tottenham, previously described the Italian as a "fantastic coach", while his success at Chelsea and across Serie A demonstrates his ability to deliver under pressure.

However, Conte is unlikely to accept the job without significant backing, and that is where United's biggest problem remains.

Whoever replaces Carrick will inherit a lop-sided squad with major holes to fill, so January investment will be essential if the club wants an immediate improvement, rather than simply relying on a change of manager to transform its fortunes.

Conte could certainly shake things up at Old Trafford, but United must be prepared to give him the tools to do so.

#1939. ST MIRREN 0 RANGERS 2: It's back to the grind for McInnes' men as they show grit to see off Buddies

By KEVIN MCKENNA AT MARBILL COACHES STADIUM

Published: 17:42 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 17:51 EST, 7 November 2026

At some stage, you would suspect Rangers are going to find their groove under Derek McInnes.

But until then, they will happily settle for just getting points on the board. How they go about it doesn’t really matter in the grand scheme of things.

This hard-fought victory in Paisley — much like so many of Rangers’ Premiership wins this season — was all about substance over style.

Yes, there were flashes of quality here and there. But it was more to do with doing the ugly stuff well than anything else. Fortunately for McInnes, his side are proving to be adept at doing so.

It’s a handy habit to have at their disposal. We saw it in recent draws at Dundee and Hearts last month, managing to come away with something when they probably deserved nothing.

With nobody knowing what version of Celtic are going to turn up on any given week, all Rangers can do is stay within touching distance of the league leaders — a point in front ahead of their meeting with Kilmarnock this afternoon — until they come to blows again in the new year.

Rangers skipper Neil nets with the aid of a deflection to put his side two goals up

Rangers wasted no time getting themselves on the front foot. St Mirren barely got a kick in the opening exchanges, and on the odd occasion they did, possession was turned over far too easily.

Badredine Bouanani had the visitors’ first effort of the night on six minutes, cutting inside from the right flank before pulling the trigger from 20 yards, but it lacked the power to properly test Jacob Chapman in the Saints goal.

The keeper had to be far more alert five minutes later, pulling off a wonderful reaction stop to deny Ryan Naderi finishing off Kevin Kelsy’s headed knockdown. You would have put your house on the in-form Czech finding the net.

Emmanuel Fernandez headed over from the resulting corner.

Having finally settled down, St Mirren gave their opponents a perfect opportunity to take the lead, when Samuel Ramos brought down James Penrice on the angle of the Buddies’ box.

There didn’t appear to be a great deal of contact, but it didn’t take long for VAR to confirm referee Nick Walsh’s decision.

Naderi stepped up to do what he failed to do moments earlier, coolly slotting into the bottom corner to register his ninth goal in all competitions this season.

From looking as if he was likely to be on his way out of Ibrox over the summer, the 23-year-old has become one of the first names on McInnes’ team sheet.

Penrice goes down under Ramos' challenge to earn Rangers a penalty in the first half

And perhaps the most exciting thing from a Rangers perspective is that he is still a million miles from being the finished article. But playing with this sort of confidence, he’s only going to get better.

He was involved in a lovely free-flowing counter shortly after the half-hour mark, with the ball eventually falling to Kim Min-su on the penalty spot. However, the South Korean delayed getting his shot off and the chance was gone.

When running full-flight at defences, the 20-year-old is a delight to watch in that No10 role.

There isn’t anyone in the country better at finding pockets of space between the lines and taking the ball on the turn. But for all that there is to enjoy about his game, his decision-making in the key moments undoubtedly needs work.

A woeful ball out from Olwethu Makhanya set up a two-v-two for the hosts before the break, with Ramos drilling straight at Ivor Pandur from inside the area. With the whole goal to aim at, the Spaniard should have done much better.

The same goes for Jake Young, who blasted high and wide from a promising position a minute later.

Naderi is hailed by Min-su after putting the visitors ahead from the spot

As dominant as Rangers were, you never got the feeling their lead was particularly secure, such is their tendency to play themselves into trouble every now and then.

Fernandez is the worst culprit for it. Fortunately for him, his recovery pace gets him out of jail more often than not. He needed it on a couple of occasions here.

A delightful threaded ball from Bouanani found the feet of Min-su inside the box on 47 minutes but under heavy pressure, he was unable to prod beyond Chapman who’d rushed off his line to meet him. It was hard to be too critical of the Rangers midfielder this time.

Chapman was once again called into action to thwart Kelsy from close range after the Venezuelan escaped the clutches of his marker to collect Min-su’s pass in behind.

He then skewed an effort wide at the back post from an excellent Nico Raskin delivery from the right. It was a night on which very little came off for the big man in front of goal.

To his credit, he kept plugging away, and played a key role in Rangers’ doubling their advantage just after the hour mark, with his driving run causing a bit of chaos in the Buddies backline, before captain Dan Neil swept a loose ball into the bottom corner via the aid of a big deflection to give Chapman absolutely no chance of saving.

With his first touch, substitute Eseosa Sule wasted a glorious chance to reduce the deficit after being left all alone at the back post to stab home Declan John’s cross.

With the ball seemingly destined for the back of the net, Rangers keeper Pandur produced a stunning save on the stretch to turn the ball round the post.

The Croatian’s signing went somewhat under the radar over the summer, but he has demonstrated time and time again that he is a man for the big occasion. He’ll win this side plenty of points between now and the end of the season.

McInnes applauds the away support after signing off for the international break with a win

St Mirren came into this one having won just once in their past eight, but you wouldn’t have guessed they were struggling for confidence given the way in which they threw everything at the game in an effort to get a result.

It wasn’t for lack of trying, with Luke Thomas testing Pandur from range before Calvin Ramsay’s follow-up header clipped the post.

That would be as close as Saints would come, as Rangers dug in to grind out an ugly — but ultimately deserved — win on the road.

They will need to be far better, far more consistently if they want to get their hands on the Premiership title come May. But that’s a worry for another day.

#1938. Chelsea urged to sign Trent Alexander-Arnold amid Liverpool return rumours

Chelsea have been urged to sign ‘top-class’ Trent Alexander-Arnold in January following a frustrating start to his Real Madrid career.

Alexander-Arnold completed a dream move to Madrid last year, ending a 21-year spell at boyhood club Liverpool in which he won two Premier League titles and the Champions League.

The England international featured in a little over half of Real Madrid’s league games last season as the Spanish giants endured a rare trophyless campaign.

Competition at right-back only increased over the summer with the arrival of Denzel Dumfries from Inter Milan and Jose Mourinho is currently playing midfielder Federico Valverde in that position.

As a result Alexander-Arnold appears to be third choice and has only earned four starts this season, with his lack of game-time raising speculation over his future at the Bernabeu.

‘Before he went to Madrid, he would have planned on nailing down his spot at right back there, and then they brought in a new right back the summer after he arrived, which will have only frustrated him further.

#1937. Sheffield Wednesday suffer new injury blow as Dave Challinor learns more about what he has in reserve

He needs to know what he has by way of depth too, as injuries continue to strike at Hillsborough, with Max Lowe the latest senior player to fall foul of one, ruled out for the next six weeks.

All that was up for grabs between the Owls and Accrington Stanley on Tuesday was which team would have a home tie in the last-32 as group winners, and it was the League Two side who took it with a 4-0 win.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Wednesday used the opportunity to protect senior players, having a debut to Louis Poland and substitute James Kay, plus a first start to Denny Oliver.

It showed in a disjointed performance in only Challinor's second game in charge, the first being Sunday's FA Cup exit at the hands of League Two Oldham Athletic.

"I suppose it's what I expected really, the one thing it has done it means I've seen pretty much every player over the time I've been at the club in terms of first-team fixtures, youth-team fixtures, and a mixture today," he said. "But understanding of where priorities were and what was most important.

"Some young players have made their debuts and it was a really proud moment for them and things that they'll remember.

"Obviously the challenges which there's going to be but for all of them they should be better for the experience whether it's good or bad and should stand them in good stead hopefully moving forward on the start of their journeys."

With only 5,472 in attendance at Hillsborough on a cold night and no real jeopardy, the match was played in a subdued atmosphere.

"It's tough because it almost becomes like a pre-season game really where you're expecting there to be little cohesion because you're chucking a group together that don't train together on separate sites, put together really last minute in terms of what it looked like," said Challinor. "It was probably making decisions on some players even within the group we've got whether they're able and some injuries.

"We had to make structured substitutions so I went into it not expecting loads, understanding what it would look like and probably you have to get yourself in that headspace as early as possible so as not to become frustrated because young players especially are going to make mistakes. Some of the more senior ones in terms of minutes and football are still very young and still make mistakes.

"That was probably what the game looked like from our perspective. To run through a few that may or may not be on the fringes of the first team."

One big plus for George Brown was his first appearance of an injury-hit 2026, leading the line before making way at half-time.

"It was a tough comeback for him because an experienced centre-half who's been round the block and we played pretty direct into him."We told Connal (Trueman, the goalkeeper) if it was on to play, play, but can we play over, especially for the young lads early on and try and get them a feel. George had a right fight on his hands but he's got through 45 minutes which is brilliant."

Former Sheffield United defender Lowe suffered another hamstring injury in Sunday’s defeat at Oldham.

"Max has got a recurrence of the injury he had earlier in the season, so he's going to be out for a period, probably maybe four to six weeks," confirmed Challinor. “It’s disappointing because you saw the impact and the profile of him in terms of what we want to try and do in possession.

"That's disappointing for everybody, but something that we'll have to deal with.”

Sean Fusire captained the side from right wing-back, but will miss Saturday's League One game at home to Plymouth Argyle on international duty with Zimbabwe.

"He hasn't got the vaccinations to go to Equatorial Guinea," where Zimbabwe play on Thursday. "The plan is I think he travels tomorrow (Thursday) for the game on Sunday (the reverse fixture in the African Cup of Nations qualifiers), and Kieran (Morrison) and Jordi (Liongola) are away as well."
