#1835. AFC Wimbledon vs Blackpool - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 11 Nov 2026 14:40, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 14:46

Returning to League One action after competing in the opening round of the FA Cup, AFC Wimbledon welcome Blackpool to Plough Lane on Saturday afternoon.

The Dons suffered a 2-1 defeat to League Two outfit Crewe Alexandra last weekend, while the Seasiders survived a scare against Hornchurch, needing a 118th-minute winner to book their place in the second round, where they will face Salisbury.

Playing their first league match since Halloween, Johnnie Jackson and his Wimbledon side will be desperate to end a run of six league games without a victory, and 10 matches without a win across all competitions, when they take on a Blackpool side they have avoided defeat against in each of their previous five meetings.

With that said, the Dons are unlikely to have entered any previous meeting with the Seasiders in worse form than they find themselves in currently, having followed a 1-0 victory over Doncaster Rovers on September 12 with three league draws and six defeats, while also suffering early exits from the EFL Trophy and FA Cup during their difficult spell.

Taking on high-flying Stockport County at the end of October, Wimbledon entered the final stages with a one-goal advantage but conceded late strikes from Jack Diamond and Ethan Ennis to suffer another damaging defeat, before facing Crewe last weekend as favourites to progress in the FA Cup.

However, their journey in football's oldest competition came to a premature end as they suffered a 2-1 defeat against fourth-tier Crewe, with Charlie McNeill producing a memorable moment by scoring from the halfway line inside the opening 12 minutes.

With no further cup commitments until next season, Jackson and his side can now focus entirely on their League One campaign as they look to rediscover some much-needed form and move further away from the relegation zone.

As for Blackpool, they avoided an FA Cup upset at the weekend when they faced National League outfit Hornchurch, although Ian Evatt's side were forced to take the scenic route before eventually booking their place in the second round after extra time.

The Seasiders went into the break a goal behind but emerged with renewed purpose and soon drew level through a sweetly struck Jordan Brown volley, before Josh Bowler struck deep into extra time to spare their blushes and prevent what would have been a significant cup upset.

That victory means Evatt's side are now unbeaten in three matches, following an EFL Trophy win over Aston Villa Under-21s and a 1-1 draw away to Sheffield Wednesday, who spent the majority of that league encounter with 10 men.

While just one defeat in their last five matches across all competitions represents a notable improvement for the Seasiders, they still head into their 13th League One fixture of the campaign dangerously close to the relegation zone.

Three wins, three draws and six defeats have given Blackpool a slender one-point cushion over 21st-placed Wigan Athletic, although they do have games in hand on several of the sides immediately above them, while a victory this weekend would see them leapfrog Wimbledon, who currently sit 18th on 13 points.

Following the disappointing defeat to Crewe, Jackson could make a number of changes to his starting XI, although Wimbledon emerged from the cup tie without any fresh injury concerns.

Andy Yiadom came off the bench on Saturday and marked his appearance with a goal, potentially earning himself a starting opportunity for this fixture, with Isaac Ogundere among those most at risk of dropping out.

The Dons remain without forward Mathew Stevens, who continues to recover from a hamstring injury that has kept him sidelined since March.

Stevens scored 26 league goals for Wimbledon across the previous two seasons and has since been replaced by Jayden Stockley, who has impressed during his maiden campaign at the club and is expected to lead the line again as he looks to add to the six League One goals he has scored in 13 appearances.

Blackpool also had a substitute make an immediate impact last time out, with Bowler finding the net from the bench to strengthen his case for a return to the starting XI in London.

Fraser Horsfall made his long-awaited return to action at the end of October in the EFL Trophy but suffered another setback and is set to miss a third consecutive match, having last started a game in April.

The Tangerines are also without Irish midfielder CJ Hamilton and 33-year-old defender Michael Ihiekwe, who are recovering from knee ligament and muscle injuries respectively, while George Honeyman and Niall Ennis are also expected to remain in the treatment room, adding to Evatt's growing list of absentees.

In the absence of captain Honeyman, Karoy Anderson is expected to wear the armband in the centre of midfield.

Bursik; Tilley, Yiadom, Johnson, Seddon, Sasu; Smith, Harrison, Hippolyte; Stockley, Cornick

Peacock-Farrell; Williams, Lyons, Casey, Ashworth, Coulson; Bowler, Morgan, Anderson; Bloxham, Taylor

With these two sides separated by just a single point in the League One table, we expect Saturday's meeting to be a closely contested affair, particularly given that both clubs are in need of points to improve their respective positions.

Wimbledon have struggled to find consistency in recent weeks, but Blackpool's own defensive vulnerabilities could give the hosts an opportunity to end their winless run, and we expect the sides to share the spoils after an entertaining 2-2 draw.

#1834. Michael Carrick reveals club bosses have not told him if he will still have a job next week, with Man United languishing in relegation zone ahead of Aston Villa clash

Published: 17:30 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 04:50 EST, 8 November 2026

Michael Carrick has not been given any guarantees over his future beyond Sunday's game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford as Manchester United dropped into the relegation zone.

United bosses handed Carrick more time to turn the club's season around following the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth a fortnight ago amid speculation he could be replaced by Eddie Howe or Julian Nagelsmann.

In the two games since then, Carrick's side have lost at Chelsea and staged a rousing comeback over Roma in the Champions League to secure a first win in 10 games.

United slipped into the bottom three after Nottingham Forest beat Manchester City on Saturday, and could be in last place by the time they kick off against Villa depending on the outcome of other games involving Sunderland and Crystal Palace on Sunday.

The situation could leave Carrick's position under threat during the two-week international break. Asked if he has been told outright that he will be in charge next week, the United boss replied: 'No. Just carry on as absolute normal.

'Whatever is going to happen is going to happen. I'm really looking forward to the next game, playing at home on the back of the other night.

Michael Carrick revealed that club chiefs have not told him if he'll be in charge next week

Sir Jim Ratcliffe (left), Omar Berrada (centre) and Jason Wilcox (right) have not informed their manager about their plans for the international break

'The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming energised and feeling good about what they might see, and we've got to repay that.'

Carrick is preparing for a normal international break, and doesn't have any plans to spend more time with his family after a turbulent period at Old Trafford.

'Not really different to normal. Genuinely not,' he added. 'I think international breaks are always a time to re-energise and freshen up. Some of the players that go away to internationals get freshened up in a different environment, but I don't really need it. I'm fine as I am.

'We'll certainly train next week and maybe have the weekend off. We'll see how that develops, who's left behind, who's with us and what they need.'

Carrick insisted that he and Bruno Fernandes have put any issues behind them after the United captain criticised his tactics in the Champions League defeat to Como last month.

After he led United's fightback against Roma in midweek by converting a twice taken penalty, Fernandes confirmed that Carrick's decision to drop him for the Bournemouth game was due to a loss of form, and disputed that the two men had a clear-the-air meeting over his comments.

But Carrick said: 'There are always conversations, bits going on; acknowledging certain things of when things are going well, what we need to improve on as a group.

'Sometimes it's individually, sometimes it's group. We always have discussions. What's actually said in that discussion, I'll keep that to myself.

'But I think it's pretty clear we've moved in a good direction, and Bruno's commitment is undoubted for me (in terms) of what he brings to this team and this club.

'He showed that again this week by his actions, the way he's played and how he dealt with even retaking the penalty and the frame of mind he was in for that. I think that tells you everything. Bruno's as good as ever.'

#1833. England 2-1 Croatia: Harry Kane with the winner to cap special night

England captain Harry Kane marked his record-breaking 126th cap with a 92nd international goal as the skipper’s spot-kick sealed a 2-1 win over Croatia and set up a Nations League shootout in Spain.

The irrepressible 33-year-old enjoyed a night to remember at a sold-out Wembley, where the Bayern Munich sharpshooter’s Ballon d’Or triumph was celebrated along with his landmark appearance.

Kane became the most capped Englishman in history, having last month equalled the record held by Peter Shilton, who was on hand to make a pre-match presentation to the star along with the Prince of Wales.

The striker looked like he would be denied a customary goal on this special night as Croatia defended diligently before capitalising on a second-half error to cancel out Morgan Rogers’ opener.

Petar Sucic pounced on a poor Jarell Quansah header, but the England defender quickly won a penalty that Kane slammed home as the nation’s all-time scorer netted in a fifth successive game.

Thomas Tuchel’s men had already effectively secured qualification for March’s Nations League quarter-finals before this match, but Thursday’s victory rubberstamped it and kept hopes alive of winning Group A3 heading into Sunday’s trip to leaders Spain.

Kane makes sure it’s business as usual on his special night for England

Slaven Bilic’s side were restricted to long-range efforts in a forgettable first half that took 16 minutes for the hosts to muster a shot through Elliot Anderson.

Trent Alexander-Arnold saw a drive blocked and Luka Vuskovic prevented Kane meeting a cutback from Rogers, who soon converted one provided by Jude Bellingham.

Kane clipped a diagonal pass over to the Real Madrid star, whose first-time ball bobbled through for the stretching attacking midfielder to strike into the ground and past Dominik Livakovic.

England failed to kick on after taking a 24th-minute lead and the crowd thinned, with half-time refreshments proving more appealing than the performance. The absence of added time spoke volumes.

Kane was stopped from scoring England’s second of the night six minutes into the second half as Josip Stanisic got in the way of a low Declan Rice ball.

Bellingham saw an attempt denied and Anthony Gordon tried his luck before England gifted Croatia a way back.

Josko Gvardiol was there to help bundle on a corner that Quansah attempted to nod back to Joran Pickford, only for Sucic to capitalise on the weak header and slam home in the 59th minute.

It was a costly defensive mistake, but the England centre-back soon benefitted from one at the other end after Ivan Smolcic wrestled him to the ground at a corner.

Referee Morten Krogh was sent to the monitor and awarded a penalty that Kane thumped home in the 64th minute.

Sucic was denied another leveller as Croatia looked to respond, with both sides making changes to alter the dynamics.

Ben White was among those introduced and booed by some of the England faithful. Croatia veteran Luka Modric received a far warmer reception.

Nikola Vlasic went close as the visitors pushed and Quansah blocked an Ante Budimir shot after James Garner was denied a first England goal by an offside in the build-up.

Budimir went close in stoppage time, but England held out as attention turns to Madrid.

#1832. Who can England face in Nations League quarter-final? Next opponents confirmed ahead of Spain showdown

England are on course to record their best ever performance in the Nations League, having beaten the Czech Republic twice and Croatia during the autumn international break.

Including its inaugural season in 2018/19, the Three Lions have competed in every single Nations League campaign, experiencing some highs and the lowest of lows.

From topping their group and qualifying for the Nations League finals and finishing third to suffering a shock relegation in 2022/23 and then immediate promotion, England have done almost everything except win the competition.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign with a loss to Spain, despite leading 2-1 at one stage, England bounced back in style by beating the Czechs twice and then thumping Croatia 7-0 in a remarkable, record-breaking rout. Another win over Croatia followed at Wembley on Thursday night to confirm a top-two finish in the group and qualify for the Nations League knockout stage.

England now face a one-game shootout with Spain to decide who will win the group, and an easier quarter-final tie next March.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - would be kept apart.

As things stand, if England finish second in Group 3, their potential Nations League quarter-final opponents would be Italy, Netherlands or Portugal.

Topping the group would set up a possible quarter-final showdown with France, Greece or Denmark.

The draw for the 2026/27 Nations League quarter-final will take place on Friday, November 20 with the ties scheduled to take place in March 2027.

#1831. ​Women’s Super League predictions: Chelsea backed to edge top-of-the-table showdown

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

The Women's Super League table is starting to take shape as the campaign reaches its 10th matchday, and there are plenty of intriguing fixtures on the schedule this week.

Manchester City replaced Chelsea at the top of the tree last week, as the defending champions routed West Ham 5-0 and Sonia Bompastor's Blues were held to a frustrating draw by Everton.

And as City and Chelsea prepare to go head-to-head at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, both teams have a chance to land an early blow in the title race.

London City Lionesses are lurking in third ahead of the weekend's action, and they are involved in one of three derbies to take place on Sunday.

While Alexia Putellas and company face Arsenal in another star-studded clash, there is also a second city derby between Aston Villa and Birmingham City, and an East London grudge match between West Ham and Charlton Athletic.

But who will be the winners and losers? With the help of the Opta supercomputer, we delve into the pre-match insights.

How the #BarclaysWSL table looks after Matchweek 9  Which result had the biggest impact on the standings?  #LeagueStandings | #WTWKicks https://t.co/a69A5f6R6Y

— Barclays Women's Super League (@BarclaysWSL) November 8, 2026

The Progress with Unity Stadium hosts the early kick-off on Saturday, with Manchester United hoping to continue their revival under Eva Olid.

After going unbeaten in their last 11 games in all competitions (W8 D3), United could equal their club-record unbeaten streak, having enjoyed sequences of 12 matches without losing ending in March 2023 and February 2026.

They are assigned a 71.8% chance of beating Crystal Palace – the highest win probability assigned to any team on MD10.

The Eagles' hopes of an away win are rated at a mere 12%, and United are the only team to face newly promoted sides more than twice in the WSL and never lose such a game, winning all 15 of those matches by an aggregate score of 43-5.

Palace should be buoyed by their 3-2 victory over Charlton on MD9, but this will be Palace's 32nd match in the WSL, and they are yet to win consecutive games.

The weekend's headline fixture takes place shortly afterwards at Stamford Bridge, as Chelsea and Manchester City go head-to-head for top spot.

This is the first WSL season to see two teams remain unbeaten after nine matchdays since 2020-21 (Chelsea and Man Utd on that occasion).

And this will be the third instance of two unbeaten sides meeting at least 10 matchdays into a campaign, after 2020-21 (Chelsea 2-1 United on MD11) and 2018-19 (City 2-0 Arsenal on MD10).

Chelsea suffered their joint-second-heaviest WSL defeat when they last met City in February, going down 5-1 at the Etihad Stadium with the since-departed Kerolin scoring a hat-trick. However, the Blues have not lost back-to-back league games against the Citizens since a run of four defeats between 2015 and 2017.

And Opta's predictive model makes them favourites on home turf this week, with a 49.1% win probability.

City's hopes are rated at 25.3%, while the 25.6% likelihood of a draw is the largest assigned to any game this weekend.

If Chelsea are to come out on top, they will have to keep a close eye on Khadija Shaw, who should be well-rested after being left on the bench throughout City's 4-1 victory over Inter in the Women's Champions League.

Recapping our first win in Europe this season  https://t.co/YkVAGV7omA

— Manchester City Women (@ManCityWomen) November 11, 2026

Shaw has 12 goals in nine WSL games this season, with only Vivianne Miedema (14 goals for Arsenal in both 2018-19 and 2019-20) ever netting more in a team's first 10 matches of a campaign. And Shaw could become the third player to net in 10 consecutive WSL starts, after Sam Kerr in November 2021 and Beth England in September 2020.

Chelsea will also need to start being more clinical in attack, following draws with Everton (1-1) and Hacken (0-0). The Blues have had 215 shots in the WSL this term, with their per-game average of 24 being the most by any side in a single campaign in the competition.

Tottenham are flying high in fourth place following back-to-back wins, and the Opta model fancies them to get the better of Everton. Saturday's hosts are assigned a 51.4% chance of taking all three points, with Everton's win probability only estimated at 22.3%.

Since the start of last season, only Man City (16) and Chelsea (12) have won more home WSL matches than Spurs' nine, and they could now win six home games in the competition within a single calendar year for the first time.

Additionally, since the start of May, only City (31), Chelsea (29) and Arsenal (23) have accumulated more WSL points than Tottenham (22).

And Everton will have to be particularly wary of their hosts' set-piece prowess; no team in the WSL can better Spurs' six goals from dead balls in 2026-27, which is already just one fewer than they scored from set-plays throughout the entirety of 2025-26 (seven in 22 matches).

Everton have spent just 6% of their total WSL game time in the lead this season, accounting for 48 minutes and seven seconds. Only pointless Charlton have led for a lower share of their time on the pitch (3%) and for fewer total minutes (28 minutes, 54 seconds).

No fresh injury concerns ahead of Saturday's trip to the capital, with Inma Gabarro continuing her progress. https://t.co/3pwpSaCXTW

— Everton Women (@EvertonWomen) November 12, 2026

In Saturday's late kick-off, Liverpool will look to halt their slide down the table when they take on Brighton at the American Express Stadium.

Liverpool have gone five WSL matches without a win since overcoming Everton in September's Merseyside derby.

It has been a case of style over substance for the Reds, who are completing an average of 466 passes per game in the WSL this season – their most in a single season.

Liverpool's 58.2% possession average is also their second-highest in a campaign, behind their 58.9% in 2013, while their 84.9% passing accuracy is also their best in a season.

And, with Brighton winning their last three home games in the WSL and chasing four straight victories on their own turf for the very first time, the supercomputer favours the hosts.

Across 10,000 pre-match simulations conducted by the model, Brighton won 49.2% to Liverpool's 25.3%, with the remaining 25.5% of scenarios seeing the points shared.

Local bragging rights are on the line in all three of Sunday's games, starting with Aston Villa's clash with Birmingham City at Villa Park.

Though Villa sit ninth in the table and Birmingham are 13th, only four points separate these rivals, so the visitors could drag their neighbours into the relegation battle.

Harvesting the energy for the Second City Derby  Watch Jill and Lynn on the Villa Podcast now!  https://t.co/1LIW5LcioZ https://t.co/5L9z9TNMzt

— Aston Villa Women (@AVWFCOfficial) November 12, 2026

However, Birmingham are winless in their last three meetings with Villa across all competitions (D2 L1) since a 1-0 away win in the WSL in November 2021.

And with home advantage on their side, Villa are assigned a 49.9% chance of victory, compared to a 24.8% probability for Birmingham.

However, there are reasons for positivity if you are from the blue side of Birmingham, as Villa have lost six of their last nine home WSL matches (W1 D2), conceding an average of 2.6 goals per game in that sequence.

And only Man City star Shaw (12) has scored more WSL goals this season than Birmingham's Oceane Hurtre (seven).

The only players to net more times in a campaign for a newly promoted team are Beth Mead in 2015 (12 for Sunderland), Katie Lampson in 2022-23 (nine for Liverpool) and Amalie Thestrup in 2023-24 (nine for Bristol City).

Having failed to pick up a point through nine games, Charlton are the only side below Birmingham going into this weekend's fixtures.

And if they are to stop their season from truly unravelling, a victory over West Ham at Victoria Road Stadium may be a must.

Charlton could become the first team to start a WSL season with 10 straight defeats, having already made the joint-worst start in the competition's history (Leicester City also lost their first nine matches in 2021).

West Ham, meanwhile, have already won two London derbies in three attempts this season (L1), overcoming London City (2-1) and Palace (1-0).

That is as many victories as they managed in their previous 14 WSL games against fellow capital clubs (W2 D2 L10).

Following a 4-1 victory over Liverpool in their last home WSL match, West Ham are backed by the supercomputer to win back-to-back home games for the first time since February 2025 – they won 58.6% of our pre-match sims, compared to Charlton's 19.9%.

The action concludes at the Emirates Stadium with a huge matchup between Arsenal (64.2%) and London City Lionesses (16.7%), who are truly in the mix for Champions League qualification.

Next stop: The Emirates  https://t.co/45igQcc1R4

London City enter MD10 three places and six points above the Gunners, who have endured a difficult start to the campaign, though they come into this game having held onto a point in a 1-1 draw with Barcelona in the Champions League.

And Arsenal's struggles have been particularly pronounced at home, where they have drawn four straight WSL matches, becoming the first team to do so in the competition's history.

Only in 2014 (D2 L4) have the Gunners dropped points in five different home matches in a single WSL campaign.

They do have a perfect record against London City, though, winning all seven of the sides' head-to-head meetings in all competitions, by an aggregate score of 22-1.

But London City should certainly make things difficult, having gone unbeaten in their last three away WSL matches (W2 D1), scoring 12 goals across that span.

That is just one fewer goal than they managed in their first 12 away matches in the WSL combined (13), while only Chelsea (17) and Spurs (14) have more away WSL goals this season than their 13.

History could be made by Kadidiatou Diani, who has either scored (three goals) or assisted (three) on each of her first four away appearances in the WSL.

She is just the second player to achieve that feat, after Mead in 2015, and no player has registered a goal involvement in their first five WSL away outings.

#1830. Harry Kane makes sure it’s business as usual on his special night for England

As Manchester United again dominated the headlines with their latest managerial dice-roll, Harry Kane made sure he wouldn’t be overshadowed.

On a night that was all about England’s greatest goalscorer, on his record-breaking 126th cap, Kane made sure it remained all about Kane. And rightly so.

England’s No9 pulled the lever, scored the winner, and set up a tantalising showstopper on Sunday. Whoever wins between England and Spain this weekend will finish top of their Nations League group, and with it an easier quarter-final opponent in March.

Just 17 days after winning the Ballon d’Or, being crowned the finest footballer on the planet, Kane overtook Peter Shilton at Wembley to claim the all-time England appearance record for himself. Shilton, Kane’s family and Prince William were all on hand to celebrate with him.

And how better to mark the occasion, than with the winning goal. A penalty struck down the middle was typical of a 33-year-old in a hurry to hunt down further records, still relentlessly hard-working and keen to prove that the autumn of his career can show him to be even more influential for club and country.

He has the most goals in England’s history, this his 92nd, and now the most caps, too; the England records just continue to tumble for Kane. Most goals at major tournaments. Most goals in a calendar year. Most appearances as captain. Most games won. Most, most, most, most.

Yet for a long time this was a night that was going England’s way, but not Kane’s. And then when Petar Susic seized on a Jarell Quansah mistake to equalise, the celebrations were at risk of ending early.

Choose the right education path for your child

The greatest players share that uncanny, and slightly freakish, ability to bend an occasion in their own direction. This was a night all about England paying tribute to its greatest player on the night, as he continues to do the business on the pitch.

Morgan Rogers’s goal assisted by Jude Bellingham in the first half was the outstanding moment of quality in the final third, but England were impressive in other areas, and Kane epitomised that.

A standout early moment saw him pop up at left-back to collect from goalkeeper Jordan Pickford, he then angled a frankly ridiculous long, raking pass from right-back across the entire pitch diagonally for left winger Anthony Gordon.

And then he stayed calm amid the noise — all of it about him — to clip his penalty down the middle for his first goal, for club or country, since last month’s golden moment: his official recognition, less than nine miles away, as the greatest player in the world.

#1829. Singapore vs Paraguay - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 11 Nov 2026 15:30

Singapore will be looking to get back to winning ways when they welcome Paraguay to the National Stadium on Friday.

The hosts currently sit 149th in the FIFA World Rankings, while Paraguay are 116 places above them in 33rd.

Singapore's clash with Paraguay will be their first outing since a crushing 6-0 defeat to Malaysia back in October.

That result capped a disappointing FIFA ASEAN Cup campaign, where they finished third in Group A with three points and failed to reach the playoffs.

Head coach Gavin Lee is using this international break to freshen up his squad, handing a first senior call-up to 21-year-old midfielder Woo Chun Wei and also recalling Saifullah Akbar, Joshua Pereira and Darren Teh.

The game against Paraguay will be followed by another friendly against five-time World Champions Brazil just four days later, with Lee viewing the fixtures as valuable preparation for the 2027 Asian Cup.

Describing them as a "significant challenge" for Singapore, Lee urged his players to "embrace the discomfort" and "work towards arriving at the Asian Cup as the best possible version of ourselves".

Paraguay arrive in Singapore after winning both of their post-World Cup friendlies, picking up a 2-0 win over Bolivia and a 1-0 win over Colombia.

Miguel Almiron bagged a brace against Bolivia, taking his international tally to 12 goals, while Hugo Benitez netted the winner against Colombia on his senior international debut.

Head coach Gustavo Alfaro has selected a 27-man squad for Paraguay's tour of Asia, which includes a trip to Japan following the friendly against Singapore.

Alfaro included four uncapped players and a further 11 names with less than 10 international appearances as he continues to assess his options following the World Cup, which saw Paraguay knocked out in the round of 16 by France.

Singapore are missing the likes of Ikhsan Fandi and Nur Adam Abdullah through injury, while Cardiff City defender Perry Ng will not make his international debut as he is expecting the birth of his first child.

Ilhan Fandi is set to lead the line, with support out wide from Song Ui-young and Glenn Kweh.

Paraguay, meanwhile, could hand Benitez a start with veteran striker Antonio Sanabria currently out injured.

Almiron and Ipswich Town star Julio Enciso are expected to start on the wing, with Mathias Villasanti, Matias Galarza and Damian Bobadilla set to feature in midfield.

Mahbud; Pereira, Harun, Baharudin, Stewart; Kweh, Shahiran, Stewart, Nakamura, Song, Fandi

Gill; Caceres, Gomez, Alderete, Alonso; Villasanti, Galarza, Bobadilla; Almiron, Benitez, Enciso

Singapore will benefit from home advantage, but Paraguay should have too much individual quality and we are backing them to pick up the win.

#1828. Moretto: Tresoldi ‘arrived at Casa Milan’ to sign but move collapsed – the background

Nicolo Tresoldi could have already been an AC Milan player now, given that he was very close to signing a few years ago.

Tresoldi has found himself in the Milan orbit for a number of reasons in recent weeks. His continued declarations of love for the Rossoneri – his boyhood team – already had some fans clamouring to try and sign him, and that was before his Champions League hat-trick against Inter at San Siro.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the past few days, the speculation has ramped up regarding an attempt by Milan. Not put off by the painful negotiations to sign Charles De Ketelaere and Ardon Jashari, it seems Gerry Cardinale wants to try and sign yet another Brugge star.

Matteo Moretto spoke during a video on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, and he explained that the young striker was even close to signing for Milan previously, while waiting to see what the future holds.

“In the summer of 2021, Tresoldi arrived at Casa Milan because he had every intention of signing for Milan. Milan had already closed on him,” he said (via MilanNews).

“At the time, the Maldini-Massara duo were the ones at the helm. The deal was done, all that was missing was the signatures. Tresoldi didn’t sign that day: he returned to Germany, and Milan never closed the deal.

“In the summer of 2021, Milan came close to signing Tresoldi, but he then extended his contract with Hannover. We’ll see if he can become a popular option for the Rossoneri in the future.”

#1827. Mauricio Pochettino contract details confirmed ahead of Manchester United announcement

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission.

Mauricio Pochettino has agreed a two-and-a-half-year contract to become Manchester United manager, with an official announcement imminent.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach is set to replace Michael Carrick on a deal which will run until 2029.

The Athletic reported on Thursday evening, hours after Carrick was sacked, that Man Utd will pay Pochettino’s $10million (£7.4m) to buyout clause to release the Argentine from his contract with the United States national team.

Carrick and his coaching staff were dismissed on Thursday, clearing the way for Pochettino to take charge. The deal is not yet complete, but the 54-year-old is expected to sign a contract running until 2029.

An announcement could come as early as Friday, although Pochettino is expected to remain with the United States for their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti on Saturday and Tuesday.

He would then travel to England ahead of taking charge of Man Utd’s trip to face Liverpool, at Anfield, in Premier League on November 22.

United are 18th in the table and in the relegation zone after winning only one of their opening 10 league matches this season. That run led to Carrick's departure, despite his permanent appointment only coming in May. He lasted 16 games in the role.

#1825. Next Man United manager: Why Darren Fletcher could be set for interim head coach role while Red Devils wait for Mauricio Pochettino

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 15:56, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 16:04

USA are reportedly still expecting head coach Mauricio Pochettino to lead them into their two November internationals against Haiti.

Pochettino has allegedly come to an agreement with Manchester United over personal terms and is set to become their new head coach, should Michael Carrick, as expected, be sacked.

As of Wednesday afternoon, there is still no communication from Man United over a departure for Carrick, but the Englishman is set to lose his job over the next 24 hours.

Pochettino is the red-hot favourite for the role at Old Trafford, and it is understood that an agreement in principle with the Argentine's representatives has been reached.

However, according to The Independent's Miguel Delaney, there is "still some way to go".

The publication claims that the United States are expecting Pochettino to lead them into their two matches against Haiti on November 14 and November 18 respectively.

Man United, though, are pushing to have Pochettino available sooner, given that the team will be back in Premier League action against Liverpool on November 22.

There is allegedly an option to appoint Darren Fletcher as an interim head coach once again, should Man United be unable to conclude a deal quickly.

Fletcher, who is the head coach of Man United Under-18s, was the club's caretaker head coach in January following the sacking of Ruben Amorim.

Man United's director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada met with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday to discuss Carrick's future.

An announcement regarding Carrick's removal as head coach could come on Thursday.

Eddie Howe, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann are all available for an immediate start and have been linked with the position at Old Trafford.

However, Pochettino has emerged as the club's number one choice.

Pochettino has a contract with the United States until the end of the 2030 World Cup, and Man United need to pay a £7.4m compensation fee to bring him to Old Trafford, with further fees required to appoint his trusted coaching staff, including assistant Jesus Perez.

A difficult start to the 2026-27 campaign has left Man United down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, winning just once in England's top flight this term.

#1824. New mum and ex-Lionesses star Mary Earps names baby boy Xander after announcing her partner's secret birth in heartwarming Instagram video

Published: 04:55 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 05:11 EST, 8 November 2026

Euro-winning Lionesses goalkeeper Mary Earps has named her son Xander after becoming a mother for the first time, having revealed this week that her partner has given birth to a baby boy.

Earps, 33, was a hero of England's Euro 2022 victory at Wembley and starred at the World Cup in 2023, saving a penalty in the final. She won BBC Sports Personality of the Year but later lost her England place to rival Hannah Hampton and retired in acrimonious circumstances.

She moved to France with Paris Saint-Germain but returned to England earlier this year - and has now welcomed her first child with her partner, Kitty Forrest.

'Welcome to the world, Xander,' she posted on Instagram, with a photograph of her newborn's hand.

In a video released on Friday, Earps said: 'I've been keeping a little secret from you all. And I don't think I can talk my way out of this one. So, I think I'm going to have to show you.

'I can't quite believe I'm writing this, but yesterday Kitty and I welcomed our beautiful baby boy into the world!

'We're absolutely over the moon and still trying to take it all in. It's been such an emotional journey getting to this point, and we couldn't be more excited to start this next chapter of our lives as a family of three.'

Mary Earps has revealed the name of her baby boy following his secret birth: Xander

Earps and her partner Kitty (second right) revealed news of welcoming a baby boy (YouTube/Mary Earps)

Earps says she will not be able to take maternity leave due to the rigors of the football season. Her team, London City Lionesses, are eight games into the new Women's Super League season and sit third behind Chelsea and Manchester City.

'I do have one eye sort of on football, which is super weird,' she said.

'In any other job, you would just be like, "Okay, bye. Taking maternity leave, whatever. Um, and you just do what you need to do." But that doesn't really work in football, because you've got games and then, if you take the day off, then you got to think about what that looks like and how that works into sort of your training schedule and the fixture calendar.

'So, it's a little bit more complicated. You can't just take annual leave whenever you want without consequence. You know, it's going to be interesting to see what the next days and weeks bring.'

Earps first revealed that she was in a same-sex relationship in September of last year but largely kept partner Kitty out of the spotlight.

Kitty is a physiotherapist who worked as the lead in her department at Manchester United Women, Earps's former club.

Earps is pictured kissing the trophy after England won Euro 2022 at Wembley Stadium

Earps won BBC Sports Personality of the Year in 2023 following her Euro heroics

In a statement at the time, Earps said: 'I've always tried to keep my personal life separate from my professional one, but it would have felt inauthentic not to include something so important to me in this book. I'm in a really happy relationship.

'The people closest to me have always known, and I feel ready and happy to share that with everyone else now.'

Earps retired from England duty in May last year after the release of her autobiography dragged up a storm with Hampton, the Chelsea goalkeeper who overtook her from understudy to become England No 1.

Earps revealed she told Sarina Wiegman that 'bad behaviour was being rewarded' after Hampton was recalled to the England squad.

#1823. Steven Gerrard identifies Lamine Yamal challenge after Messi and Ronaldo comparison

By Naim Beneddra | 11 Nov 2026 15:56

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard believes Lamine Yamal is already more advanced than Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo were at 19, but has identified the major challenge that could determine whether the Barcelona youngster eventually matches their extraordinary achievements.

The former England captain has been hugely impressed by Yamal's development, describing the Spanish international as a player capable of reaching the level established by two of football's greatest names.

However, Gerrard believes maintaining the hunger to win throughout a long career will be just as important as the teenager's natural ability.

He has also questioned whether Yamal may eventually need to move into a central attacking role to approach the remarkable goalscoring records accumulated by Messi and Ronaldo.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, Gerrard drew on his own experience of facing both players during their early years to explain why he considers Barcelona's latest academy graduate such an exceptional prospect.

Gerrard, who faced Ronaldo during the Portuguese forward's Manchester United career and encountered Messi in European competition, believes Yamal has reached an unusually advanced stage of development for his age.

"He's more advanced than Ronaldo was at 19," Gerrard said.

The former Liverpool midfielder also suggested that Yamal was further along in his development than Messi had been at the same stage, while acknowledging the challenge of sustaining that progress.

His assessment reflects the enormous impact Yamal has already made since breaking into Barcelona's first team in April 2023.

The Spain international, who celebrated his 19th birthday in July, has established himself as a central figure in Hansi Flick's attack despite continuing to operate predominantly from the right wing.

Yamal has registered 13 goals and 12 assists in 16 appearances across all competitions during the 2026-27 campaign, maintaining an extraordinary level of productivity for a player still in his teenage years.

His development has been accompanied by major international success, having helped Spain win Euro 2024 before adding the 2026 World Cup to his honours.

The winger has also finished second and third in the last two Ballon d'Or rankings, recognition of the influence he has already established at the highest level.

By comparison, Messi was still developing into a regular goalscorer during his teenage years at Barcelona, while Ronaldo's early seasons at Manchester United were defined more by his dribbling and individual creativity than the prolific finishing that would later characterise his career.

Ronaldo scored nine goals in 50 appearances during the 2004-05 campaign, a season in which he turned 20.

Yamal had already surpassed that figure at 17, scoring 18 times for Barcelona in 2024-25.

Yet Gerrard is reluctant to conclude that the Spaniard's remarkable start guarantees a career comparable to either of those legends.

For Gerrard, the central question concerns whether Yamal can retain the same ambition and consistency over the next decade.

The former Liverpool captain believes Barcelona's coaching staff and the people closest to the youngster will have a crucial role in keeping him motivated after such an extraordinary start to his career.

"The biggest challenge for him - and those around him at Barcelona - is how they keep him hungry?" Gerrard asked.

He believes Yamal must continue pursuing collective trophies and individual recognition even as success becomes a familiar part of his career.

The difficulty is particularly significant given the standards established by Messi and Ronaldo, whose greatest achievements were built upon sustained performances over many seasons.

Both players also developed into exceptional goalscorers after initially establishing themselves in wider attacking positions.

Gerrard therefore raised the possibility that Yamal's long-term evolution could involve a similar positional adjustment.

The 19-year-old is currently most influential when starting from the right, where his close control, ability to eliminate defenders and vision allow him to create opportunities for teammates.

Moving into a central position could theoretically increase his goalscoring opportunities, although Gerrard presented the idea as a possibility for later in his career rather than an immediate recommendation to Flick.

Yamal's existing production suggests that he does not need such a change to contribute heavily in front of goal.

His 25 direct goal involvements this season also underline why he continues to attract comparisons with Messi, whose development at Barcelona remains an obvious reference point.

Gerrard's comments follow those of former Barcelona loanee Marcus Rashford, who recently identified Yamal as the closest player he had encountered to Messi's level.

The Manchester United forward, who spent the 2025-26 season alongside Yamal, also expressed his belief in the youngster's potential to compete for multiple Ballon d'Or awards.

Gerrard shares that admiration, but his comparison carries an important qualification: Yamal may be ahead of Messi and Ronaldo at 19, yet matching what they achieved over the course of their careers will demand a level of consistency that remains impossible to judge at such an early stage.

#1821. Klopp baffled by further questions over Kimmich’s Germany place

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Jurgen Klopp is baffled by the debates surrounding Joshua Kimmich's role in his Germany setup, ahead of Friday's pivotal Nations League clash with Serbia.

Germany sit second in Nations League Group A2 with two games remaining, three points adrift of both the Netherlands and Greece.

Ahead of the Oranje visiting Berlin on matchday six, Klopp's side may need to beat Serbia to have any chance of reaching the quarter-finals.

But on the eve of that match in Belgrade, Klopp was frustrated to find himself fielding more questions about whether Kimmich warrants a place in his starting XI.

Kimmich started Germany's first two games under Klopp – a 1-1 draw with the Netherlands and a shock 1-0 defeat to Greece – before being allowed to leave the camp early to rejoin Bayern Munich, due to a minor fitness issue.

With Kimmich gone, Bayern youngsters Tom Bischof and Aleksandar Pavlovic started in the heart of midfield for a 2-0 win over Serbia and a goalless draw in the reverse fixture with Greece, winning plaudits for their displays.

But Klopp would rather focus on the qualities Bischof and Pavlovic bring to the team, rather than their suitability to replace Kimmich.

He told reporters: "We can't be happy about the performances of the two young players – because they have done a really good job – without that turning into a story about what it means for Kimmich?

"That's the narrative that gets created: What does this mean for Joshua Kimmich? It means nothing.

"I have a very positive view of this team. We have a very good mix in the squad. Tom and Aleks had a great game, and Kimmich wasn't there. Felix Nmecha wasn't there either, so I did not understand the debate."

A post shared by German Football (@germanfootball_dfb)

Klopp also believes having a high-pressure match so early in his tenure will be a major positive, as Germany build towards Euro 2028 off the back of a disappointing World Cup campaign.

"I'm looking forward to it. It's a test," he added. "We're doing all of this with one ultimate goal in mind: to be ready for the tournaments.

"[Friday] is a proper competitive match, and I expect it to be a very difficult game.

"It will be a real test for us to see where we stand, and how far we've come. We would obviously like to show that we've made good use of this time.

"We have a few hours left to make that happen, so that everyone can see it on the pitch. As I said, I'm looking forward to it."

#1820. Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds

Leeds United came from 2-0 down at half-time to beat Liverpool 4-2 at Soldier Field in Chicago as Andoni Iraola’s side were undone by sloppy defending in the second period.

Liverpool’s dominant first-half display was underlined by goals from Luke Chambers and Florian Wirtz. However, Daniel Farke’s men replied with four strikes in 25 second-half minutes through Sean Longstaff, Brenden Aaronson and two alarmingly similar goals from Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

🎯 "CALVERT-LEWIN ARRIVES!" pic.twitter.com/CaHOeXQn7E

🤩 "Calvert-Lewin makes it FOUR!" pic.twitter.com/mEEi882OWi

Liverpool centre-back Chambers, 22, who spent last season on loan at Charlton Athletic, opened the scoring on seven minutes, pouncing on a Dominik Szoboszlai corner which had been flicked on at the near post by Milos Kerkez.

Jeremie Frimpong, serviced by a wonderfully flighted cross-field ball by Trey Nyoni, then set up Wirtz to make it 2-0 five minutes before the break, but on the hour Leeds began their recovery when Aaronson scored following a mistake by Kerkez – who gave up possession to Ethan Ampadu in his own half.

GOAL! Aaronson pulls one back! 2-1 pic.twitter.com/tdy17cITSd

Ampadu’s long throw was flicked on to Calvert-Lewin to level the score, then minutes later Curtis Jones’s carelessness allowed Longstaff in to put Leeds in front.

🔥 "LONGSTAFF! WHAT A TURNAROUND!" pic.twitter.com/G9LvLIk0Mi

And it was a familiar story five minutes from time when Ampadu’s throw again prompted chaos in Liverpool’s back line, allowing Calvert-Lewin to steal in front of Jones and seal victory.

Liverpool return to Anfield for friendlies against Monaco and Como before they begin their Premier League season away at Newcastle United later this month.

Leeds have matches against RB Leipzig, Manchester United and Augsburg before their league campaign gets under way at Nottingham Forest.

Possession: Liverpool 57%-43% LeedsShots: 9-15Shots on target: 3-7Corners: 3-7

The final whistle is blown in Chicago and that has well and truly been a game of two halves. At half-time, Liverpool were in complete control with a 2-0 lead. However, four Leeds goals in 25 second-half minutes have given Daniel Farke’s side the victory at Soldier Field. Both sides will now return home to the UK.

Aaronson is booked for a cynical pull on Ramsay.

Koumas should score for Liverpool. He is played in behind and for some strange reason Cairns comes a long way out of his goal. Koumas should lift it over Cairns and into the empty net but gets his chip wrong and the shot goes off target.

Leeds’ second half gets even better and Liverpool’s gets even worse. It is a very similar goal to Calvert-Lewin’s first; Ampadu’s long throw is flicked on and Calvert-Lewin meets it, heading past Mamardashvili. This is very much your game of two halves.

Daniel Farke is making a double change as Gnonto and Lienou come on.

Frimpong kicks the ball out of play and he may have a problem. Is it just cramp or more serious than that? He is going to come off and be replaced by Scanlon.

Leeds have come from 2-0 down to lead 3-2 in Chicago. Aaronson’s cross from the left side of the box should be cleared by Jones but he does not put his foot through it. Instead, that allows Longstaff to slot home past Mamardashvili. Leeds have scored three goals in a quarter of an hour.

Leeds are on level terms. A long throw from Ampadu out on the left is flicked on at the near post and Calvert-Lewin has the easiest of tap-ins at the back post. Liverpool were in cruise control at 2-0 up at the break but not have not been at it since half-time.

Justin is played in behind down the left channel and tries to pick out Calvert-Lewin in the centre of the box but Ndiaye steps in with a crucial interception.

Andoni Iraola is going to make a quadruple change. Elliott, Ramsay, Ndiaye and Tsimikas all come on. Szoboszlai is one of those to head off and hands Jones the armband.

Liverpool were much the better side in the first half but have not really been at the races since the break.

Leeds punish Kerkez’s error and get a goal back. Kerkez gifts the ball away inside his own half and Ampadu picks up not far outside the Liverpool penalty area. He spots the run of Aaronson to his left and slides it into the American, who takes one touch before sliding it underneath Mamardashvili and into the Liverpool net.

Wilson is fouled down Leeds’ right and he will take the free-kick. The Welshman clips it in and picks out Calvert-Lewin, whose header goes well wide of the target.

Calvert-Lewin gets a touch past Ndukwe just inside the Liverpool half and drives towards the Liverpool penalty area. It is difficult to know whether it is a shot or a cross from Calvert-Lewin and the ball goes wide of the far post. Bogle did make a run towards the back post and was hoping Calvert-Lewin would pick him out.

Liverpool negotiate a couple of long throws and a corner from Leeds in quick succession.

After Ndukwe’s pass inside his own half is intercepted, Justin decides to shoot from range but Mamardashvili easily saves.

Liverpool have made a number of changes at the break, with Chiesa, Jones, Gravenberch and Koumas all coming on. It takes an absolute age for Leeds to re-emerge, with Liverpool coming back out from the tunnel nearly ten minutes before Leeds. What on earth is going on in the Leeds dressing room at the break? This is ridiculous from Leeds.

The second half begins more than 20 minutes after the first ended. To be exact, 23 minutes is the gap. Calvert-Lewin is one of a few changes at half-time for Leeds, as is former Liverpool man Wilson. We are back under way in Chicago.

Jeremie 🔗 Flo 😍 pic.twitter.com/kxwhYA845Q

Andoni Iraola said before the game that Florian Wirtz would play 45 minutes in his first game of pre-season so we can expect him and Alexander Isak to come off at half-time.

Stateside Reds enjoying the action 🤩 pic.twitter.com/hfwaLmi8xB

Possession: Liverpool 60%-40% LeedsShots: 5-6Shots on target: 3-2Corners: 1-3

The first half is brought to an end and Liverpool take a 2-0 lead into the break courtesy of goals from Chambers and Wirtz.

Szoboszlai clips a delightful cross from the right all the way to the back post, aiming to pick out the run of Kerkez. A goal-kick is given, with the referee deciding the last touch came off Kerkez, but the Hungarian left-back is not happy with that decision. The replays prove why as the last touch came off Bogle.

There will be four minutes of added time at the end of this first half due to the Gudmundsson injury in particular.

Leeds have been forced into one change in this half and they might be forced into another here. As Wirtz scored, two Leeds players collided, which has resulted in Ampadu staying down and receiving treatment. The Leeds captain though does seem to be ok after receiving some treatment.

It is a lovely team goal from Liverpool to take them 2-0 up around five minutes before half-time. Nyoni’s flat ball out to the right side of the box is volleyed first time back across the box by Frimpong. Wirtz runs onto the ball and, from the penalty spot, slots the ball home past Cairns.

After Nyoni makes an interception inside his own half, Liverpool counter. The ball is shifted out to the left, where Ngumoha drives at Bogle. Ngumoha’s step-over takes him past Bogle inside the Leeds penalty area and he drives the ball across the six-yard box but no-one in a Liverpool shirt is on hand to tap it in. Should Isak have done a better job to get on the end of that one? Possibly.

Szoboszlai, who loves scoring free-kick stunners, blasts the free-kick into the wall.

Gudmundsson’s day is indeed over and is replaced by Bornauw, which could see a shift for Leeds.

Ngumoha is brought down by Bogle inches outside the Leeds penalty area out on the left. It was very, very close to being a penalty but was just outside the box. Before the free-kick will be taken, Leeds look like they will be forced into a change as Gudmundsson has gone down clutching at his right hamstring.

For the second time in a few minutes, Rodon steps in with a crucial interception. Wirtz slides a pass through into the Leeds box on the left to pick out the run of Ngumoha. Just as Ngumoha was getting his shot away from around eight yards out, Rodon slides in to intercept. However, the offside flag goes up against Ngumoha anyway.

Wirtz and Isak link up really well inside the Leeds half, with the latter putting a touch beyond one Leeds defender and runs towards the Leeds penalty area. However, Rodon steps in with a crucial interception to take it off Isak.

Nmecha scored from long range for Leeds the other day against Sunderland and he is not far off adding another long-range goal to his pre-season tally. His effort from just outside the box is dragged just wide of Mamardashvili’s right post.

Frimpong drives forward from inside his own half and takes Liverpool through the Leeds half before he is cynically pulled down by Tanaka, who is rightly booked. Sometimes in a pre-season friendly players might get away with that but this referee does not show mercy to Tanaka.

That is nearly a horror moment for Cairns in the Leeds goal. He rolls the ball out from his own box and Isak just about gets a touch on it but fortunately for Leeds it does not end in a horror show for Cairns.

Frimpong lays it across to Nyoni in a central position outside the box and the latter takes on the shot. Nyoni goes for accuracy over power and looks for the bottom corner but Cairns gets down to his left to make the save.

Chance for Leeds. Bogle whips in a cross from the right touchline and picks out the head of Nmecha, whose effort is saved well by Mamardashvili down to his right.

Liverpool hit the front in Chicago. Szoboszlai’s outswinger corner from the right is flicked on at the front post by Kerkez and is met by Chambers, who smashes home on the half volley into the Leeds net.

Liverpool counter from their own box after defending a long throw through Isak and Frimpong, whose cross from the right is deflected behind for the first corner of the game...

The pitch is not looking in the best condition, which perhaps is not a massive surprise when you consider that Chicago Fire played here last night. They beat Charlotte 2-1, with Robert Lewandowski scoring twice.

Gudmundsson is back to his feet after some treatment but is breathing quite heavily. It does appear that the Swedish wing-back should be fine to continue.

After Liverpool clear a Leeds long throw into the Liverpool penalty area, Gudmundsson goes down clutching at his lower back after an awkward landing and play is halted.

We are under way at Soldier Field. It is not too hot in Chicago today, with the temperature a touch over 20 degrees at kick-off.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off at Soldier Field in Chicago. You’ll Never Walk Alone rings around the stadium as the teams emerge.

Liverpool: Mamardashvili; Frimpong, Ndukwe, Chambers, Kerkez; Nyoni, Szoboszlai, Wirtz; Morrison, Isak, Ngumoha.Substitutes: Woodman, Davies, Chiesa, Jones, Elliott, Tsimikas, Gravenberch, Abe, Ramsay, Scanlon, McConnell, Koumas, Ndiaye, Wright, Sonni-Lambie.

Leeds: Cairns; Justin, Muharemovic, Rodon; Bogle, Ampadu, Stach, Tanaka, Gudmundsson; James, Nmecha.Substitutes: Mahady, Ombang, Lane, Lienou, Cresswell, Bornauw, Crew, Longstaff, Aaronson, Gnonto, Pickles, Wilson, Chadwick, Mills, Calvert-Lewin, Piroe.

There was a lot to take in, during those madcap 42 seconds, but it was a scene that showed the full extent of the issues Andoni Iraola must address.

First came a handshake with Curtis Jones that the midfielder, lost in red mist, barely acknowledged. It was not impressive, shrugging off a new manager like that, but as Iraola strode across the field at Yankee Stadium, after Liverpool’s 1-0 win over Wrexham on Wednesday, the action really began.

Jones squawked and jabbed at his arm. Dominik Szoboszlai bellowed back, arms stretched out so wide you could not help but notice. Next came Kostas Tsimikas throwing the captain’s armband on the floor, landing at Jones’s feet, as Giorgi Mamardashvili and Jeremie Frimpong looked on awkwardly.

The French defender, who has arrived from Rennes this summer, is not involved for Liverpool today and is yet to feature for his new club so far this pre-season as he is eased in after a shoulder injury days after his move to Liverpool was confirmed earlier this year.

#1818. Manchester Re-United! Legends join forces to toast Sir Alex Ferguson on 40th anniversary of his appointment at Old Trafford

Published: 04:00 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 08:16 EST, 8 November 2026

Manchester United legends reunited to raise a glass to Sir Alex Ferguson on his anniversary of being named manager of the club on Saturday night.

In a decision that ushered in the most successful period in United's history, Ferguson was poached from Scottish club Aberdeen 40 years ago on Friday – with the iconic manager lifting 37 pieces of silverware during his spell at Old Trafford.

He also played a significant role in shaping the careers of a litany of stars who graced the club during his 27-year tenure, with the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Wayne Rooney and David Beckham hugely benefiting from his mentorship.

And a handful of players who shared a dressing room with Ferguson were on hand to toast the iconic manager during a celebratory evening in Manchester on Saturday night.

Diehard United fan and actor James Nesbitt shared a group photo on Instagram, featuring Ferguson alongside current United boss Michael Carrick.

Nemanja Vidic, Robin van Persie, Darren Fletcher, Jonny Evans, Javier Hernandez and John O'Shea also joined their old mentor at the bash.

Actor and Man United fan James Nesbitt posted this picture with club royalty - clockwise from front left: Jonny Evans, Darren Fletcher, Robin van Persie, Nemanja Vidic, Michael Carrick, John O'Shea, Sir Alex Ferguson, Edwin van der Sar and Javier Hernandez

Ferguson ushered in the most successful period in the club's history during his 27-year stint

Carrick has namechecked Ferguson as a crucial ally as he looks to transform United's fortunes amid the club's worst ever start to a Premier League season.

The Red Devils dropped into the relegation zone on Saturday night following Nottingham Forest's win over Manchester City, and Carrick's stint in the dugout appeared all but over following a 3-0 thumping by Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

But he was handed a reprieve by the United hierarchy and there were green shoots of optimism following a rousing 3-2 comeback victory over Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

United host Unai Emery's Aston Villa at Old Trafford today, and Carrick has admitted he has been given no guarantees on his future.

'Whatever is going to happen is going to happen. I'm really looking forward to the next game, playing at home on the back of the other night,' he said.

'The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming energised and feeling good about what they might see, and we've got to repay that.'

Carrick is preparing for a normal international break, and doesn't have any plans to spend more time with his family after a turbulent period at Old Trafford.

'Not really different to normal. Genuinely not,' he added. 'I think international breaks are always a time to re-energise and freshen up. Some of the players that go away to internationals get freshened up in a different environment, but I don't really need it. I'm fine as I am.

'We'll certainly train next week and maybe have the weekend off. We'll see how that develops, who's left behind, who's with us and what they need.'

What a fantastic evening at Old Trafford celebrating 40 years of Sir Alex taking the reign at @ManUtd. Catching up with the boys and some great speeches about how he achieved to leave such a mark on this club! pic.twitter.com/kgoNfzfPWJ

Ferguson unveiled as new manager of Manchester United in 1986

Carrick insisted that he and Bruno Fernandes have put any issues behind them after the United captain criticised his tactics in the Champions League defeat to Como last month.

After he led United's fightback against Roma in midweek by converting a twice taken penalty, Fernandes confirmed that Carrick's decision to drop him for the Bournemouth game was due to a loss of form, and disputed that the two men had a clear-the-air meeting over his comments.

But Carrick said: 'There are always conversations, bits going on; acknowledging certain things of when things are going well, what we need to improve on as a group.

'Sometimes it's individually, sometimes it's group. We always have discussions. What's actually said in that discussion, I'll keep that to myself.

'But I think it's pretty clear we've moved in a good direction, and Bruno's commitment is undoubted for me (in terms) of what he brings to this team and this club.

'He showed that again this week by his actions, the way he's played and how he dealt with even retaking the penalty and the frame of mind he was in for that. I think that tells you everything. Bruno's as good as ever.'

#1817. Cisse sheds light on Mancini’s call, impressions of Italy camp and Milan Scudetto desire

Alphadjo Cisse did his first press conference as a member of the senior Italian national team, responding to questions on a number of topics.

Cisse has been called up for the first time by Roberto Mancini, having made a sensational start to the season in his first year in Serie A, which came after recovering from a serious muscle injury that kept him out for the entire second half of last season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The 20-year-old has already scored eight goals across all competitions, with five coming in the league. The most recent of these was against Genoa on Sunday, and now there is talk of a renewal offer from Milan in order to reward his development but also fend off interest from the Premier League.

Cisse spoke at a press conference from the Azzurri headquarters at Coverciano, alongside former Milan man Mattia Liberali, with whom he played in Catanzaro. His comments were relayed by TMW.

What are your feelings after the last few months?

“I always want to demonstrate my qualities. I’ve had some very intense months and I hope to have many more like them.”

What are the strengths and weaknesses of Liberali?

“His play, his shooting. His final pass is one of his best qualities. As for his flaws, I’d say he’s a bit touchy.”

Did you expect to be the top scorer among Italian players?

“Last year’s injury was a difficult time, but I handled it well. I was very confident about coming to Milanello to showcase my skills, and that helped me a lot. Choosing Catanzaro in 2025 was a very easy decision. Polito and Aquilani wanted me, and it was the right choice. I needed playing time.”

“I can play anywhere in attack. As for the specific role, I don’t know if it’s better to say. I like playing in all positions.”

What impression did entering Coverciano give you?

“It’s great to be here, a great responsibility. We’ll have the opportunity to get to know each other in the coming days.”

“My teammates welcomed me very well, but there’s certainly a big difference between Serie B and Serie A. I owe Aquilani a lot, he’s given me a lot and given me a lot of confidence. I’m sorry for him [after he was sacked by Sassuolo], but he’ll definitely have a great coaching career.”

You’re more about talent than physicality, is anything changing?

“Quality is always important. Now in Italy, many young players are emerging, and we’re trying to give them more confidence.”

“For Milan, winning is the priority, the Scudetto like any other competition. Winning is the norm and you can’t neglect any competition. At Milan you have to win everything.”

“Every coach has left me with something. Aquilani had a huge impact last year. Mancini? He welcomed me and encouraged me to train well. Baldini helped me a lot, even though I only worked with him for two weeks. He left me with a lot.”

“Modric would be too obvious… I say Gila.”

Are you aiming to start at San Siro against France?

“The coach will decide. I’m a guy with a lot of ambition, and being here with the national team is a source of pride.”

What kind of game do you expect against France?

“They need no introduction, but Italy always aims to win. Qualifying for Italy should be the norm.”

“Without a doubt, Balotelli, he’s always been a point of reference for me in the national team.”

Do you feel ready to be a point of reference here right away?

“I like pressure, and I think I’ve got the strength to handle it. There are some important players here, some of them have won the European Championship, and you have to show respect. You have to take things one step at a time. The first thing to focus on is making your debut, and then we’ll see.”

#1816. Thibaut Courtois reveals how Jose Mourinho has changed since Chelsea

By Naim Beneddra | 11 Nov 2026 16:14

Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois has revealed that Jose Mourinho is a calmer and less intense manager than the one he worked under at Chelsea 12 years ago, although the Portuguese coach has lost none of his commanding personality.

The Belgium international, who won the Premier League under Mourinho at Stamford Bridge in 2014-15, has been reunited with his former manager following the latter's return to the Santiago Bernabeu during the summer.

Their second spell together has allowed Courtois to observe how Mourinho's approach to managing players has evolved, particularly in the dressing room.

Speaking to Sky Sports during the Web Summit in Lisbon, the 34-year-old suggested that experience has made the former Chelsea boss more measured in his dealings with players.

However, Courtois believes Mourinho's authority remains unmistakable and even suggested that his arrival provided precisely the kind of presence Real Madrid needed.

The goalkeeper also shared an unusual story about their reunion, revealing that he accidentally ignored Mourinho's first message for two weeks while representing Belgium at the 2026 World Cup.

“I think sometimes he’s a bit more calmer” Thibaut Courtois on Jose Mourinho's managerial style at Real Madrid compared to how he was at Chelsea ⏪ https://t.co/9HGnNSTzE2

Courtois was part of the Chelsea squad that secured the Premier League title during Mourinho's second spell in west London, having returned from his loan spell at Atletico Madrid in the summer of 2014.

The pair worked together during a successful 2014-15 campaign, when Chelsea also won the League Cup, before Mourinho left the club in December 2015.

More than a decade later, Courtois believes the Portuguese coach has developed a slightly different approach to handling the demands of an elite dressing room.

"I think he himself says he has maybe grown to be more mature," Courtois explained.

"And with the experience, I think sometimes he is a bit calmer.

"At Chelsea, I remember he was a bit stronger in the dressing room, a bit more intense. Also now he is, but I feel he is a tiny bit less from what I remember from 12 years ago."

The Belgian nevertheless stressed that Mourinho continues to command the attention of everyone around him.

"But he's still the same personality, the same presence," he added.

"He fills the room. When you come in and he's there, you feel he's there. I think that is something that we needed."

Those comments offer an insight into how Mourinho has been received by one of Madrid's most experienced players following his return to the Spanish capital.

The 63-year-old began his second spell at the Bernabeu after Madrid endured a trophyless 2025-26 campaign, with Courtois among the senior figures already familiar with his methods.

Mourinho's side have recovered from two early La Liga defeats to establish an eight-match winning streak across all competitions.

That sequence includes a 2-1 victory over Barcelona at Camp Nou on October 25 and last weekend's 3-0 success against Valencia.

Madrid have also won their opening four Champions League matches, leaving them well placed to secure direct qualification for the knockout stages.

In La Liga, they sit three points behind leaders Barcelona after 12 matches, having accumulated 30 points from 10 victories.

Despite his enthusiasm about working with Mourinho again, Courtois admitted their reunion began with a communication mishap.

The goalkeeper was away with Belgium at the World Cup when Mourinho first attempted to contact him following his appointment at Real Madrid.

However, the message arrived while Courtois was travelling, and he failed to notice it amid the disruption caused by the flight and the time difference.

"He texted me when he arrived in Madrid, but I ignored his message for two weeks," Courtois revealed.

"We were at the World Cup at the time, and the day he texted me, we were on a plane."

The Belgian explained that the lack of Wi-Fi meant several messages went unnoticed, with the misunderstanding only becoming clear when Mourinho contacted him again after an international match.

"Later, after a match, he texted me again, and I asked someone at Real Madrid, 'Is this the coach's number?' But everything is fine now."

The incident did nothing to diminish Courtois's enthusiasm about their reunion.

The goalkeeper explained that he and Mourinho had parted on good terms when the manager left Chelsea and that he had been looking forward to working under him again.

For Courtois, the most significant change is not in Mourinho's authority but in how he exercises it.

That assessment comes at an encouraging moment for Madrid, who will attempt to extend their winning sequence when they host Celta Vigo on November 21 following the international break.

The reunion has already produced positive results, and Courtois's account suggests that Mourinho has found a balance between the demanding management style that defined his Chelsea years and a more measured approach at the Bernabeu.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

Lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

Chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.
